articles.title_orig: Hurricane Isaias live updates: Gulf Coast evacuations expand with expected Category 3 landfall
articles.title_zh: Hurricane Isaias live updates: Gulf Coast evacuations expand with expected Category 3 landfall
articles.content_orig:
States of emergency have been issued in parts of Alabama, Florida and Georgia, and up to 9 feet of storm surge is possible.
⛈️🌊 Track the storm, check your local risk and get more detailed timing from meteorologists in the CNN Weather app
• Tropical storm conditions have started in the Gulf Coast ahead of Hurricane Isaias’ expected landfall “at or near” Category 3 strength around Pensacola, Florida, tonight.
• Storm surge up to 9 feet is possible and up to 15 inches of rain. 1.7 million people in the Florida Panhandle and parts of Alabama and Georgia are under a tornado watch .
• Mandatory evacuations have been ordered in counties in Florida and Alabama, and several cities – including Mobile – are implementing curfews. The White House said President Donald Trump has canceled plans to attend the Alabama-Georgia football game in Tuscaloosa.
• Isaias is expected to cause widespread power outages and disrupt travel, with some airports , bridges and rail services closing during the storm. Nearly three-quarters of the Gulf’s daily oil output has also been derailed.
From late Friday afternoon through midnight, Isaias’ dangerous conditions will begin to affect the Gulf Coast as the large storm churns northward.
Hurricane Isaias is expected to strengthen significantly over Thursday and Friday. Even if it weakens slightly before landfall, the storm will remain dangerous along the Gulf Coast.
Hurricane Isaias is due to make landfall late Friday night into Saturday as a strong Category two storm. A state of emergency has been declared across Florida and Alabama.
Meteorologist Ali Van Fleet explains how a weakening hurricane can still grow in size and threaten a broader region with rain, storm surge and even tornadoes.
All hurricanes are dangerous, but their impacts aren't always created equal. Meteorologist Chris Warren explains how storm size and storm strength influence the impacts communities experience before, during and after landfall.
To help people prepare for hurricanes, scientists studied 40 tropical cyclones and found storm surge hits in eight ways.
President Donald Trump will no longer attend the University of Alabama vs. University of Georgia football game in Tuscaloosa Saturday as Hurricane Isaias threatens the area, a White House official told CNN.
Trump previously said he was going to “let the hurricane” determine his decision to attend the rivalry matchup. “If there is an emergency or if there’s a hurricane, I don’t want to do anything to take the focus off all of the great people that work on those things,” he said.
Expected to make landfall Friday night on the Gulf Coast, Isaiah has strengthened into a Category 3 storm with winds between 111 and 129 mph.
Alabama could see harsh winds, soaking rain and storm surge, prompting states of emergency to be issued in some areas.
Hurricane hunters transmit “Vortex Data Messages,” public summaries which include important information about a hurricane’s eye, including pressure, wind speeds, shape and also … the species of birds flying in it.
Birds often are spotted in the eye of intense hurricanes since it’s a place of relative calm compared to its surroundings. The most recent message noted that hunters saw, specifically, white egrets.
North Carolina Gov. Josh Stein and emergency officials are urging residents to “prepare, don’t panic” as officials and residents brace for Hurricane Isaias’ impact.
While the storm is not expected to make landfall in North Carolina, the governor warned in a Friday news release that localized flooding and gusty winds are possible this weekend.
“Make sure you are signed up for local emergency alerts, prepare an emergency kit in case you lose power, and do not drive through flooded roads,” Stein said. “Take care of your loved ones, and check on your neighbors too.”
State emergency response teams and rescue resources are being positioned ahead of potential impacts, according to the news release.
Officials are urging residents to take proactive steps to protect themselves and their families:
Hurricane Isaias will pick up speed when it moves ashore, which will affect which parts of the Southeast are most impacted by this storm.
Surface winds typically weaken once a hurricane is over land, but a faster-moving storm can carry its powerful winds farther inland.
This effect will likely be especially pronounced just east of where Isaias makes landfall. With the storm traveling north, the winds on its eastern side will blow in the same direction as the storm is moving — the combined speed will create stronger winds on that side.
Despite multiple warnings from officials, people were still seen walking along the beach early Friday afternoon on the Santa Rosa Island Authority’s “East Cam” live feed.
Santa Rosa is a barrier island located along the Florida Gulf Coast and spans three counties: Escambia County, Santa Rosa County and Okaloosa County — all of which are expected to be affected by Hurricane Isaias.
The area is no stranger to flooding. In 2004, the entire island was flooded by Hurricane Ivan, according to the Santa Rosa Island Authority .
Even as Isaias is expected to make landfall later tonight along Florida’s Panhandle, an Alabama mayor is warning residents to prepare as a curfew is set to take effect.
“It could still make a turn if it needs to. We all remember what Sally did to us,” he said, referring to the Category 2 hurricane that hit Alabama’s Gulf Coast in 2020.
Orange Beach has a curfew beginning at 7 p.m. CT Friday until 7 a.m. CT Saturday, Kennon said. He encouraged residents to stay indoors.
Tropical storm force winds are beginning to spread onto coastal areas along the Florida Panhandle as well as southern Alabama as Hurricane Isaias moves closer to land, according to the National Hurricane Center.
At 1 p.m. CT, the storm’s center was located 145 miles south of Pensacola, Florida, and it was moving north-northeast at 16 mph.
A wind gust to 47 mph was recently reported at Dauphin Island, Alabama, the NHC reported. These winds are arriving along with the storm’s rain bands, making any additional last-minute storm preparations more difficult for coastal residents.
“Preparations against life-threatening storm surge and devastating winds should be completed in the next couple of hours,” the NHC warned.
Alabama Power has brought in 5,700 additional resources from 25 states to support in response to the approaching storm.
Isaias could cause significant damage to homes and roofs, and cause widespread power outages across the state, officials have warned.
The utility company is urging residents to download the Alabama Power app to report any outages and encouraging people to stay clear from downed power lines.
Santa Rosa County issued an evacuation order for an additional area Friday morning. Other areas of the county have been under evacuation since 12:30 CT Thursday.
There are roughly 11,855 residential structures in the evacuation areas, Tom Lloyd, Santa Rosa County Public Safety Director, told CNN.
The county evacuation shelter was housing more than 60 people and 8 animals as of 11:00 AM CT Friday, he said.
Two bridges going in and out of Gulf Shores, a coastal resort town in Alabama, have been shut down, CNN’s Isabel Rosales reported live from the area on Friday.
“I spoke with a city official who also told me the time to prepare is now closed.” Rosales told CNN News Central Anchor Boris Sanchez. “He told me it is time to find your permanent place to hunker down.”
Gulf Shores is expected to get up to 6 feet of storm surge with 6 inches of rain or more, according to the National Hurricane Center.
A tornado watch is in effect for nearly 1.7 million people in the Florida Panhandle, far southeast Alabama and far southwest Georgia until 9 p.m. ET.
Tallahassee, Florida, is included in the watch area.
Storms embedded in Hurricane Isaias’ rainbands are moving north and will spread across the area, likely spinning up a few tornadoes. The twisters are likely to be EF2 or weaker

articles.title_zh: EXCLUSIVE: US imposes sanctions on ICC hours after former judge wins Nobel Peace Prize
articles.content_orig:
The ⁠ICC’s deputy prosecutor condemned the sanctions and said they would not halt the tribunal’s work
Navi Pillay has begun giving a press conference after the declaration that she has won this year’s Nobel Peace prize. She began by saying she dedicates the award to “survivors of international crimes”.
She called on people to stand together in the defence of rule of law.
And, on that note, we will be closing the blog for today .
The Nobel peace prize has been awarded to Navi Pillay, the South African former UN human rights chief who chaired the UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza ( 11:02 , 11:04 , 11:06 , 11:11 ).
In her first reaction, Pillay specifically paid tribute to all people defending human rights everywhere, as she joked to her associates that “if you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump” ( 11:53 , 12:02 ).
Her win was widely celebrated by senior judges and human right campaigners, who offered their congratulations ( 11:33 , 12:06 , 12:17 , 12:21 , 13:22 , 15:25 ), including the president of the international court of justice, of which she is a former judge ( 12:58 ).
But Israel reacted angrily to the award, saying that “it’s the grotesque weaponisation of an award to legitimise anti-Israel hatred and prejudice” ( 13:52 ).
US president Donald Trump also reposted a critical comment saying the Nobel committee “shamed itself beyond repair and demeaned” the prize ( 16:06 ).
Just hours after the announcement, which was explicitly meant as the Nobel Committee’s backing for the international court of justice, the US has imposed sanctions on the court ( 16:20 ).
If you have any tips, comments or suggestions, email me at jakub.krupa@theguardian.com.
I am also on Bluesky at @jakubkrupa.bsky.social and on X at @jakubkrupa.
When the British government announced sweeping sanctions on trade with illegal Israeli settlements and condemned “ethnic cleansing” in the West Bank by state-backed “settler terrorists”, some EU diplomats hoped this dramatic shift in UK government policy towards Israel would have a galvanising effect on the rest of Europe. So far, it has not.
Although France and Canada joined the UK in pledging to ban goods from illegal settlements and impose sanctions on “those who facilitate them or profit from them”, there has not yet been a wider ripple effect.
A meeting of EU foreign affairs ministers on Monday is likely to showcase the bloc’s stasis in policy towards Israel – a stalemate that is at odds with rising public criticism in Europe of Israel’s government.
A survey of 10 European countries, including Spain, France and Sweden, found large majorities of people had a negative opinion of Israel. Views had become more negative compared with the previous year, according to the Pew Research Center, mostly after the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran, which unleashed a new crisis in the Middle East and a global economic shock. In Poland, negative views jumped eight points to 70% of respondents, in Italy they increased by nine points to 75% and in Germany they also rose by nine points to 73%.
Israel is facing ever deeper isolation in the theatre of public opinion. Five countries chose to boycott the Eurovision song contest this year over Israel’s participation, after organisers declined to exclude it over its conduct in the Gaza war and rising violence in the West Bank. Organisers have now decided that broadcasters will no longer be eligible to host the song contest if their state is involved in an armed conflict or sensitive geopolitical situation.
More than 74,000 people, including at least 21,200 children, have been killed in Gaza since Israel launched its war in retaliation for the Hamas attack of 7 October 2023, in which the terrorist group killed 1,209 people – including 36 children – and took 251 hostages, inflicting a nationwide trauma .
Gaza remains a humanitarian catastrophe , with people facing acute shortages of water, nutritious food and medical equipment and medicines, while contending with disease, unemployment, economic collapse and the threat of death or injury. Israel’s airstrikes continue: the death toll includes 1,400 Palestinians killed since a ceasefire was declared a year ago.
The EU talks on the Middle East will focus on the conflicts in Iran and Yemen, but ministers will also discuss the situation in Gaza and the West Bank in the context of elections in Israel on 27 October and the first legislative elections in Palestine in 20 years, which are expected by late November.
The discussion is expected to expose familiar fault lines in the 27-member EU. One group of countries are vocal supporters of the Palestinian cause: Spain and Ireland were the first to call for a review of whether Israel’s conduct in the Gaza war was in breach of the human rights requirements of its association agreement with the EU, which covers the €68bn (£58bn) trade relationship, cooperation in research, environment and energy.
A second group consistently opposes targeting Israel’s government: Germany and Austria are close allies for historical reasons, while Czechia and Italy are ideologically aligned with Benjamin Netanyahu’s administration.
Among a third, larger group of countries in the middle are several, such as France and the Netherlands, that are increasingly critical of the Netanyahu government’s conduct in Gaza and its plans to build the vast E1 settlement, which threatens to critically damage the two-state solution.
Czechs go to the polls on Friday at the start of two days of voting to fill one-third of the seats in Parliament’s upper house, the Senate, and elect local representatives, AP reported.
The elections are the first test for populist billionaire Andrej Babiš since he returned to power after a decisive victory in parliamentary elections in October 2025.
His centrist ANO (YES) movement hopes to make gains in the 81-seat Senate, which is controlled by pro-western opposition parties. Twenty-seven Senate seats are up for grabs in the two-round election, with runoffs scheduled for next week. First-round results are expected on Saturday.
Babiš has formed a governing coalition with two small political groups whose agenda includes reducing support for Ukraine and rejecting some key European Union policies.
Unlike the government, the opposition and president Petr Pavel remain firm supporters of Ukraine following Russia’s invasion.
But Pavel – an avid biker – attracted a lot of attention in the build up to the vote as it emerged that he would miss the vote due to a long-planned motorcycle trip in Morocco. After days of relentless pressure, he eventually cut the holiday short and reported to vote, acknowledging his original “error” in scheduling.
“Some mistakes can be corrected relatively easily, others with more difficulty, and some cannot be corrected at all.
Fortunately, a mistake in planning can be remedied by changing the plan. Admitting a mistake is not easy, but if a politician values people’s trust, he must prove it.
I know what responsibility is and that any trust is hard to earn, but terribly easy and quick to lose. You pay for mistakes, and I have learned from this one of my own.”
The European Union is granting temporary trade preferences to Armenia following trade restrictions recently imposed by Russia.
In a move which shows how flexible the EU can be, it said the temporary trade preferences “will help alleviate the difficult situation faced by Armenian producers and exporters and support the resilience of Armenia’s economy by facilitating access to the EU market.
The measures, which will enter into force tomorrow for a period of two years, temporarily allow 80% of Armenian exports to the EU, including almost all exports of fresh fruit, vegetables and flowers affected by the Russian measures, as well as over 91% of exports of beverages and spirits.
Armenia is not an accession state, but has been singled out for support as part of the EU a broader solidarity support package

articles.title_orig: Katie Zacharia Picked as the New White House Press Secretary
articles.title_zh: Katie Zacharia Picked as the New White House Press Secretary
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump has selected conservative commentator Katie Zacharia to serve as the next White House press secretary , he announced Friday.
Zacharia will replace Karoline Leavitt , who stepped down in August, in the position.
Zacharia currently works as a communications adviser at Trump Media and Technology Group, the company that runs Trump’s social media platform Truth Social. She previously worked at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) as a spokesperson for former Secretary Kristi Noem, and appears frequently on conservative media including Fox News and Newsmax.
In a post on Truth Social announcing his selection, Trump praised Zacharia for “an unblemished record of support” and being “a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning.”
“She is, likewise, a devoted fan and member of MAGA!” Trump continued. “I am confident that Katie will deliver strong results for our Country as the next White House Press Secretary, as she has the respect of, and will work fantastically with, the Media, the American People, and my Administration.”
The New York Times first reported that Zacharia had been tapped by the White House.
Zacharia, who currently lives in California and graduated from Pepperdine Caruso School of Law, has also worked as a general counsel for almost three years at Fix California, a conservative non-profit founded by Ric Grenell, who served as Acting Director of National Intelligence during Trump’s first Administration. The organization works to promote a conservative agenda around the state.
In June, Zacharia was appointed to the advisory board of NovaRed Mining Inc, a Canadian mining company based in Vancouver, according to a company announcement . Just a week before Zacharia’s appointment, Noem also joined the advisory board.
Leavitt, who became the youngest White House press secretary in history at the age of 27, this week joined Fox News as an on-air contributor, the network announced on Monday. She is the third of Trump’s former press secretaries to join the network. She begins on Nov. 1.
Trump announced Leavitt’s departure through a Truth Social post in which he said that she “will now be one of my top outside advisors, and an influential voice within the Republican Party, as we work to defy History, and conclusively win the Midterm Elections.”
Leavitt responded with a lengthy post on X in which she thanked the President and the White House and said that she would remain “a vocal advocate for MAGA and the Republican Party. ”
Leavitt gave birth to her second child, Viviana, in May. She went on maternity leave that month and later announced that she would be stepping down from her role to spend more time with her family.
Trump’s time in office has been characterized by a contentious relationship with the media, which he has repeatedly attacked and derided while serving as President. Leavitt echoed that attitude during her time behind the podium, becoming known for her acerbic remarks and quick deflections during press briefings.
Zacharia will enter the White House during a fight over the media’s access to the President. Trump on Sept. 18 banned POLITICO, CNN, and MS NOW from the White House grounds, sparking an ongoing legal battle. Though the outlets’ access to the White House has been restored after a federal judge issued a temporary restraining order against the ban, Trump has since restricted POLITICO and CNN from boarding Air Force One, preventing them from carrying out their White House pool duties and drawing further blowback.
Zacharia would also be entering the White House at a time when Trump is facing record-low approval ratings over his handling of the war in Iran, which has contributed to rising inflation in the U.S., and as the fast-approaching November midterms threaten Republicans’ control over both chambers of Congress.

articles.title_orig: Trump, Putin reach deal to release Russian diesel to world
articles.title_zh: Trump, Putin reach deal to release Russian diesel to world
articles.content_orig:
US President Donald Trump says he has reached an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin allowing Moscow to "immediately release" diesel into the global market.
He said Putin had agreed to release 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and another million after that.
"Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!" Trump wrote on Truth social.
An envoy to Putin welcomed the deal, but Ukraine's president said any easing of sanctions on Russia played into Moscow's hands and would prolong a war that must be ended.
Diesel prices in the US have doubled since the war with Iran began in February, putting pressure on Republicans ahead of the midterm elections over the rising cost of living.
The average diesel price in the US is currently $6.28 a gallon, according to the AAA, down from the record high of $6.53 recorded at the the end of September.
Shortly after Trump's announcement, the US Treasury formally issued a temporary license allowing Russian diesel into the market.
An envoy for Putin, Kirill Dmitriev, welcomed the deal on social media, saying: "Russia-US co-operation on diesel and energy will benefit the world."
But Volodymyr Zelensky hit out at the deal, saying "gifts to Putin will not work for peace" and that Russia would repay the diesel with "further terror".
"Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged," he wrote on social media.
This year Russia has experienced two waves of severe fuel shortages across the country as a result of Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries.
According to the International Energy Agency, its diesel production is estimated to have fallen by nearly 30%.
Trump has expressed his displeasure over those attacks, blaming them for rising fuel prices.
But on Friday Zelensky defended the strikes, saying there were in response to "Russia's years-long campaign of terror against Ukraine's energy sector".
"Ukraine will not set Russian oil refineries on fire if Russia does not destroy our energy infrastructure," he said.
What impact the deal with Russia will have on fuel prices remains unclear. The global benchmark for crude oil, Brent, remains above $103 a barrel. Before the war with Iran, Brent crude was trading at about $73 a barrel.
The BBC has contacted the White House for comment on what reimbursement the US is providing Russia in return for the release of diesel.
It is the latest effort from the president to lower fuel prices in the US.
Earlier this week, Trump said he was "thinking about" suspending the federal tax on gasoline, and also announced that he would allow so-called red dye diesel to be used on US highways without facing federal tax.
He has also successfully pressured G7 nations into releasing 100 million barrels of oil and diesel from stockpiles to help ease supply concerns, and previously supported calls for a ban on diesel exports from the US.
Trump wants to reduce the cost of fuel as the midterms loom - will it work?

articles.title_orig: Powerful quake hits Panama, damages homes; canal operations normal
articles.title_zh: Powerful quake hits Panama, damages homes; canal operations normal
articles.content_orig:
Hazardous waves are possible as far south as Ecuador and as far north as Mexico, as 13 aftershocks reported
A powerful 7.6 magnitude earthquake has struck Panama and triggered tsunami warnings along the west coast of Central and South America, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS).
The quake hit along the southern coast of the country, the USGS said. It was centered near the southern tip of the Central American country, about 14km (9 miles) south-west of the remote community of Pitaloza Arriba, the USGS said.
The Institute of Geosciences of the University of Panama said the quake struck at just before 1pm local time near the southern town of Tonosí. The Panamanian institute said that a second 6.0 magnitude earthquake struck soon after, at 1.22pm.
By 1.3opm there had reportedly been 13 aftershocks.
The president, José Raúl Mulino, said he had asked a key minister to call for calm. “What happened should not be used to generate alarm and disorder,” Mulino wrote on X.
Local newspaper La Prensa said that across the Central American country, buildings, schools and homes were evacuated as a result of the “powerful movement of the earth”.
Footage published by La Prensa showed severe damage to several buildings in the city of Penonomé, including the St John Baptist Cathedral. Other photos showed a highway to the west of the capital that had been completely sheared in half by the earthquake.
Tremors were felt strongly ​in the ⁠capital of ⁠Panama ​City, ‌according ‌to ‌witnesses who spoke to Reuters. The Associated Press reported that buildings shook and visibly shaken residents gathered outside as they waited for news of the quake’s impact.
The USGS said hazardous waves were possible along the coasts of Costa Rica, Ecuador, Peru, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador and Mexico, although the tsunami warning for Chile was cancelled at 4.18pm local time.

articles.title_orig: 7.6 earthquake strikes Panama
articles.title_zh: 7.6 earthquake strikes Panama
articles.content_orig:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A powerful 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck off Panama's southern coast Friday, shaking the country's capital as officials investigated a potential tsunami threat.
The U.S. Geological Survey initially measured the earthquake at magnitude 8.0 before lowering its estimate to 7.7. The quake struck at 1:56 p.m. ET, approximately 6 miles beneath the surface, near Pitaloza Arriba, Panama. A 5.5 magnitude aftershock followed, with its epicenter approximately 50 miles east of the initial earthquake.

People stand outside the maternity ward of the Santo Tomas hospital, following a severe magnitude 8 earthquake thet hit the country, in Panama City on October 9, 2026. (Photo by Martin Bernetti/AFP via Getty Images)
The earthquake was felt in Panama City and in San José, the capital of neighboring Costa Rica, according to Reuters.
Tsunami officials warned that waves reaching 3 to 10 feet above tide levels were possible along some coastal areas of Panama, while parts of Ecuador could experience waves of approximately 1 to 3 feet.
Smaller tsunami waves of less than 1 foot above tide levels were forecast for coastal areas of Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Mexico, Nicaragua and Peru.

articles.title_orig: Top Democratic Group Pumps Millions Into Kansas Senate Race
articles.title_zh: Top Democratic Group Pumps Millions Into Kansas Senate Race
articles.content_orig:
Democrats are dreaming of a revolution in Kansas in November, trying to believe in polling that shows a tight race in the Senate contest there between the Democrat, Rev. Adam Hamilton, and the Republican incumbent, Sen. Roger Marshall.
It would indeed be a watershed moment if Hamilton takes the seat: No Democrat has won a Senate seat in Kansas since 1932, not quite a century but a very, very long time.
In fact, since Kansas became a state in 1861, only three Democrats have represented it in the Senate. It’s a remarkable statistic since the two parties have evolved so much during that time.
Related: Read a Q and A with a Kansas-based political expert from CNN’s What Matters newsletter about why Kansas has stayed Republican at the Senate level for so long and why Kansans feel targeted by some of Trump’s policies this year.
While American politics seem locked in place; 30 of the 50 states have been represented by a senator from both parties during this century. And while the states that have been represented by both parties most recently track closely with the swing states that decide elections, there are a few exceptions, like Montana and Alabama.
No Republican has been elected to represent the islands since 1970. That Republican, Hiram Fong, was one of Hawaii’s two first senators, elected when Hawaii became a state in 1959. No Democrat has been elected to represent Wyoming or Utah since that same year.
The longest streak east of the Mississippi River is in New Jersey, where no Republican has been elected to the US Senate since Clifford Case was elected in 1972, capping a long career on Capitol Hill. A Republican senator, Jeffrey Chiesa, was briefly appointed to serve in 2013. That was the result of the state having a Republican governor, Chris Christie, at the time.
The Senate is up for grabs. Plot each party’s best path to winning
A Kansas voter would have to be well over 100 years old to have voted for the state’s last Democratic senator, but the current governor is a Democrat.
In New Hampshire, the state is represented by two Democratic senators. The last Republican elected was Kelly Ayotte in 2010. She’s currently the state’s governor. And Republicans hope that another former senator, John Sununu, can break the trend and reclaim a Senate seat this year. When he served as senator, the state had two Republican senators.
Far fewer states are sending a split delegation — both a Republican and a Democratic senator — than ever before in US history. Since the nationwide election of senators began with the 1914 election after the ratification of the 17th amendment, there have generally been at least 10 and frequently more than 20 split delegations, according to a 2021 analysis by Pew .
Currently there are only four: Vermont, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin — none of which has a Senate race this year — and Maine, where Republican Sen. Susan Collins is among the most endangered incumbents. If she loses to Democrat Troy Jackson, Maine will join the wave of states bringing their senators in line with their status as blue or red for presidential purposes. And Collins is one of the few true moderates of either party left in the chamber.
The other senator from Maine, Angus King, is an independent, but like Sen. Bernie Sanders in Vermont, he sides with Democrats in procedural matters, making him a Democrat for purposes of determining which party controls the Senate.
The last time Vermont elected a Republican, Sen. Jim Jeffords in 2000, he ended up switching parties when Republicans angered him. There’s conjecture now that Pennsylvania’s Democratic Sen. John Fetterman might soon do the inverse, but he has insisted that he will remain a Democrat.
There’s Pennsylvania precedent for party-switching. Sen. Arlen Specter went from R to D in 2009.
These rural Democrat and Republican voters have a message for Washington
The last Democrat elected to the Senate from Texas was Lloyd Bentsen in 1988. He resigned to be in President Bill Clinton’s Cabinet. 1988, coincidentally, is the last year California elected a Republican. It does not feel close — or not as close as Texas — to electing someone from the out-of-power party, but things are changing all the time.
Both Dakotas and Montana were represented by two Democrats within the last 25 years. Now all three are represented by two Republicans, although this year in Montana and South Dakota it is independents, not even Democrats, who are mounting the biggest challenge to Republicans.
The independent who seems to have the best chance of winning at the moment is in Nebraska, where Dan Osborn is challenging Sen. Pete Ricketts. A Democrat last won in Nebraska in 2006.
There are a lot of reasons that running as an independent is tricky in American politics, especially at the state or national level. Osborn’s success might not turn into a Senate seat, but it is a clear message that there are states where party brands are so badly damaged that shedding them could be the best path to unseating an entrenched in-party power. But it’s also true that as the parties change and shift, tectonic moves mean their time in power is ultimately limited.

articles.title_orig: The US and China Cannot Slow the AI Race, But They Can Make It Safer - The Diplomat
articles.title_zh: The US and China Cannot Slow the AI Race, But They Can Make It Safer - The Diplomat
articles.content_orig:
The most important shift in artificial intelligence (AI) is not that models are becoming more intelligent, but that they are becoming more capable of acting.
Much of the first wave of AI safety governance focused on misinformation, bias, deepfakes, privacy violations and harmful content. Those risks remain. But increasingly capable AI agents can plan, write and execute code, use tools, obtain credentials, and interact with external systems. Recent incidents in which OpenAI’s autonomous systems slipped past their constraints show that as agents gain tools and autonomy, the boundary between a model and the outside world becomes harder to enforce.
That makes AI safety a collective-action problem. The AI superpowers face a prisoner’s dilemma. If one laboratory slows while competitors continue, it may lose its edge. Disclosure creates a similar tension: reporting failures can make the wider ecosystem safer, but the discloser bears the costs and may expose vulnerabilities to attackers. Governments face the same strategic impasse as the firms. Washington fears that slowing its AI development will allow China to catch up; Beijing fears that doing so will leave it further behind.
Yet cooperation can be narrow on AI safety. The United States does not need to trust China, share frontier models with China, or slow its own AI development to have a national security interest in such cooperation. It has an interest in ensuring that AI-enabled cyber incidents are contained before they cascade through third countries, shared software infrastructure and global supply chains. China has the same systemic interest.
This collective action has significant implications for middle-power countries. Helping others repair a vulnerability can be a form of systemic containment and a public good.
The AI arms race is intensifying.
U.S. President Donald Trump has rejected calls to slow U.S. AI development, framing continued technological leadership as essential to winning the AI race . On September 29, he convened major technology companies at the White House, where six firms – OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, xAI and Nvidia – signed a voluntary accord built around four layers of oversight: internal capability assessments, internal audit teams, independent external auditors, and board-level review. His administration ordered federal agencies to replace the term “artificial intelligence” with “ super intelligence ,” presenting the technology as a source of economic and strategic leadership.
Taken together, these moves point to a U.S. approach combining continued AI power with developer responsibility, voluntary industry controls, external scrutiny, and ex-post legal accountability.
China approaches the problem through a more centrally coordinated system. In May 2026, guidelines on AI agents , issued jointly by the Cyberspace Administration of China, the National Development and Reform Commission, and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, made “safety and controllability” a baseline requirement for agent development and deployment. Governance is tiered, with tighter filing, testing and recall requirements for agents used in sensitive sectors.
On September 14, China’s AI Safety Governance Framework 3.0 reiterated “safety and controllability” while updating its classification of AI risks and associated technical and governance measures.
Despite their institutional differences, the two approaches converge on one point: neither country wants safety policy to halt AI development, and both increasingly recognize that greater autonomy creates new problems of control.
Common Ground and Shared Risks
AI systems rest on overlapping technological foundations. Chinese AI development has relied heavily on U.S. chips and, in some cases, U.S. cloud infrastructure. Export controls may weaken those hardware links, but the stronger case for joint risk management lies in the software and services AI systems share.
Standards, certificates, identity infrastructure, model repositories, and open-source libraries support trust across networks. A compromised root certificate or a maintainer’s credentials can put the entire dependency tree at risk .
AI risks vary along two dimensions: severity of harm and whether responsible actors can recognize it in time. The biggest danger is severe and invisible harm, where nothing visibly breaks for days or weeks, yet time compounds the severity of the incident. An AI agent could quietly corrupt records, act on instructions planted in its memory or in documents it consults, or appear cooperative while accumulating access beyond operator intent. Infrastructure may operate normally while the means to disrupt it are already in place.
The dependencies and shared risks determine which code a system runs, which credentials it accepts, and which updates it trusts. Harm can cross borders quietly even when models and their owners remain separate.
That makes the speed of response critical. Delays in detecting a breach, assigning responsibility or authorizing a shutdown can allow damage to spread. Both China and the United States therefore need warnings to reach personnel with the authority and technical means to respond.
There is no obvious diplomatic agreement that can resolve the paradox built into the AI race: it rewards speed and secrecy, while safety depends on collective restraint and disclosure.
China-U.S. cooperation should instead focus on measures that improve safety without requiring either side to slow unilaterally, transfer its most advanced models, or expose commercially and strategically sensitive capabilities. Four areas stand out:
Before the Trump-Xi summit, American and Chinese security experts in a long-running bilateral dialogue proposed red lines around nuclear systems, human control over consequential cyber operations, and a dedicated mechanism for AI incidents.
When an AI agent can search, authenticate, write code, call external tools, and act within minutes or seconds, where should human intervention occur? Requiring approval for every step would undermine the autonomous value of AI agents; waiting until something goes wrong may make intervention too late.
The harder questions concern permissions, escalation thresholds, shutdown mechanisms and which actions should always require explicit human authorization. Researchers could cooperate on these engineering challenges without sharing model weights, training data, or proprietary frontier capabilities.
Sandboxing, monitoring, permission controls, and model-level refusals are often treated as established safeguards.
The underlying technical risk is broad: with appropriate tools and access, advanced models could identify previously unknown vulnerabilities and develop exploits across well-protected systems without step-by-step human direction. The key question is not whether a developer has guardrails, but whether they still work as agents become capable enough to search for ways around them.
While frontier AI labs in the U.S. have voluntarily disclosed instances of their models escaping from sandboxed environments, public reporting from China on comparable containment failures remains limited. This lack of transparency shouldn’t stop the two sides from working together. Washington and Beijing could develop compatible methods for testing sandbox escape, scope violations, unauthorized tool use, shutdown resistance, and failures of human intervention. Independent auditors, potentially from trusted third countries, could help verify the results.
Cyber attribution has always been challenging. AI makes it harder.
A defender discovering unauthorized access may be looking at a state-directed operation, a criminal actor using AI, a human-directed autonomous agent, or an agent that has exceeded its instructions while pursuing a legitimate task.

articles.title_orig: Class action alleges Webull misled investors about China operations
articles.title_zh: Class action alleges Webull misled investors about China operations
articles.content_orig:
A class action accuses Webull of hiding the real scale of its China operations from investors.
A securities complaint filed October 8 in federal court in Tampa, Florida, alleges online broker-dealer Webull Corporation told investors one story about its ties to mainland China while the reality, according to the filing, was very different.
The complaint, Ward v. Webull Corporation et al. (Case No. 8:26-cv-03052), brings claims under federal securities laws - specifically Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act and SEC Rule 10b-5. It names Webull - a Cayman Islands-incorporated broker-dealer whose shares trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker "BULL" - along with the company's founder and CEO, and its CFO, as defendants.
The company describes itself as a broker-dealer regulated in 12 major markets globally, with US offices in St. Petersburg, Florida.
The case centers on a string of SEC filings the complaint alleges painted an incomplete picture. In its 2024 annual report, a July 2025 registration statement, and its 2025 annual report, Webull told investors its "operations in mainland China are limited to research and development and technical support functions," according to the complaint. Those filings also stated that US customer data "cannot be transmitted outside of the United States or accessed by our non-U.S. employees without permission and oversight from our U.S. personnel."
The complaint alleges those statements were "false and/or misleading." In reality, the filing claims, "Webull's core platform, software development, data pipelines, and core engineering depended on PRC-based personnel and on technology infrastructure subject to Chinese law."
More broadly, the complaint alleges that "Webull's ownership structure, technical workforce, technology infrastructure, cross-border data routing, financing, and compliance structure were structurally tied to China" - contradicting the company's assurances that its main business operations were US-based.
The numbers in Webull's own filings tell the story. The complaint points to the company's July 2025 registration statement, which disclosed that its mainland China subsidiary, Hunan Weibu Information Technology Co., Ltd., "employs 731 employees, representing 61% of our employees as of December 31, 2024." By the end of 2025, the complaint alleges, that figure had climbed to 863 employees - 62% of Webull's global workforce.
The complaint also alleges that the US House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party delivered a letter to the CEO of Webull Financial - the company's US broker-dealer arm - in December 2024, seeking information about the relationship between Webull Financial and Webull's China operations, and about the security of customer data.
According to the complaint, Webull's SEC filings characterized the Select Committee's concerns as "largely based on outdated and inaccurate information."
That position became harder to hold on October 7, 2026. The complaint alleges that before markets opened, CNBC reported the Select Committee had found a "profound gap" between how Webull presented itself as an American company and its actual control and operations. The committee also reportedly found that Webull "initially told the Select Committee that it had no offices or employees in China," the complaint alleges.
Webull's stock dropped sharply. The complaint alleges the company's Class A ordinary shares fell $1.39 per share - approximately 19% - to close at $5.89 on unusually heavy trading volume.
The complaint alleges the company's founder and CEO - a citizen of the People's Republic of China who, as of March 31, 2026, held approximately 79.2% of total voting power - "knew or recklessly disregarded" the extent of Webull's dependence on China-based operations.
For advisors and compliance teams, this complaint is worth watching. The allegations raise questions about due diligence on broker-dealer platforms with complex cross-border structures - and about what happens when a company's SEC filings and a congressional investigation tell different stories about where operations actually sit.
The allegations in this complaint have not been tested in court. No court has ruled on the merits of the case.

articles.title_orig: Nitrogen leads solid Casse quartet at Breeders’ Cup World Championships
articles.title_zh: Nitrogen leads solid Casse quartet at Breeders’ Cup World Championships
articles.content_orig:
D.J. Stable’s Kentucky homebred Nitrogen will make her third appearance at the Breeders’ Cup World Championships when she headlines a talented field in the Grade 1, $2 million Breeders’ Cup Distaff.
Trained by dual Hall of Famer Mark Casse, the 4-year-old Medaglia d’Oro bay made her last three outings in New York, including a pair of memorable Grade 1 starts at Saratoga Race Course with a 12 3/4-length romp in the Ogden Phipps presented by Ford and a runner-up effort to reigning Horse of the Year Sovereignty while facing males in the Whitney.
Her Ogden Phipps effort earned a career-best 113 Beyer Speed Figure with the Chad Brown-trained runner-up Fully Subscribed exiting that race to win three graded events, including a pair of Grade 1s.
Nitrogen had her final Breeders’ Cup prep at Belmont Park, wiring a field of five to score by 2 3/4-lengths under regular rider Jose Ortiz in the Grade 2 Beldame on September 25.
“We shipped her down to Kentucky on Wednesday and she trained this morning at Keeneland. She's doing well,” Casse said. “I thought the Beldame was a good race. I liked the timing. It looks like a showdown between her and Chad's filly.”
Casse said he has no intention of dulling Nitrogen’s abundant early foot in a Distaff field expected to have other potential pace types.
“She'll be pretty close. We may slow her down a little bit but we're not going to take hold of her. We're going to let her do her thing,” Casse said.
Nitrogen has banked in excess of $3 million through an 18-9-6-3 record that includes a trio of graded wins on turf and five graded wins on dirt. Her previous Breeders’ Cup attempts came at Del Mar, including a closing third as a maiden in the 2024 Grade 1 Juvenile Fillies Turf and a runner-up try to Scylla in last year’s Distaff.
While Casse hopes she can go one better in the Distaff at Keeneland, he’s buoyed by the fact that D. J. Stable plans to bring back the reigning Champion 3-Year-Old Filly for another season of racing next year.
“That's the plan as long as she's healthy out of the Breeders' Cup,” Casse said. “Our sport needs its stars and she's definitely a star. I commend the Greens for being the sportsmen they are.”
Gary Barber, Bridlewood Farm and Eclipse Thoroughbred Partners’ late-running Measure has hit the board in each of her last four outings – the last three in Grade 1 company – and will look to capitalize on a potential pace battle in the Breeders’ Cup Distaff.
The 3-year-old daughter of Essential Quality finished third in the nine-furlong Grade 1 Coaching Club American Oaks won by stablemate Counting Stars in July at Saratoga to begin her streak of top-flight tilts. She followed with a neck second to My Gun's Loaded in the Spa’s 10-furlong Alabama presented by Keeneland Sales on August 22 ahead of a closing third in the 1 1/16-mile Cotillion on September 19 at Parx when in tight approaching the three-eighths.
“She's a filly that we were high on from the beginning. I wasn't that disappointed with her earlier on in the year, I just thought she needed to get her act together and needed some pace,” Casse said. “Her Alabama was a huge race, and she got very unlucky in the Cotillion. She'll enjoy the mile and an eighth and will also enjoy a hot pace, which looking at the Distaff it's looking like it will be fairly lively.”
Manny Franco will retain the mount on Measure.
Gary Barber, Blue Crevalle Racing and Eclipse Thoroughbred Partners’ Classic Q was initially considered for a Breeders’ Cup start versus males in the Grade 1 Mile but will instead target the Grade 1 Filly and Mare Turf.
The 4-year-old Classic Empire grey has won 3-of-6 starts this year, including frontrunning scores in the Grade 2 Distaff Turf Mile in May at Churchill Downs and the Grade 1 Just a Game presented by Resolute Racing on June 6 at Saratoga. She secured her second career Grade 1 last out with a stalking nose score over Lush Lips in the one-mile First Lady on October 3 at Keeneland.
“We thought about the Mile but we're going to run her against the girls,” Casse said. “I would think with the mile and three-sixteenths that more than likely she'll be on the lead.”
Hall of Famer Javier Castellano takes over aboard Classic Q from fellow Hall of Famer John Velazquez, who is committed to Gimma a Nother.
D.J. Stable will also be represented by Voyager in the Grade 1 Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf.
The Justify bay ran second in her first two outings on dirt, including a runner-up try to Harper’s Corner in the Listed Schuylerville on July 3 at the Spa.
Voyager then shifted to the Saratoga turf on August 1 and stretched out to a two-turn 1 1/16-miles to post a frontrunning nose score over Correlation Trade. The third-place finisher of that event, Bittersweet Memory, exited to graduate at Saratoga and followed with a fourth-place run in the Grade 2 Miss Grillo here last weekend.
Voyager enters the Breeders’ Cup from a 1 1/4-length win in the Grade 1 Natalma contested at a one-turn mile over firm E.P. Taylor turf on September 12 at Woodbine.
Casse said the Spa turf experience will be beneficial for Voyager as she goes back to two turns for the one-mile Juvenile Fillies Turf.
“When she broke her maiden at Saratoga, I was happy because we were able to get a two-turn race into her. We went back to one-turn for the Natalma, but I feel she's very versatile. Her race in the Natalma was really good and she's training really well,” Casse said.
Casse enjoyed a winning barn debut Thursday for world-traveler Facteur Cheval , who scored by a half-length under Irad Ortiz, Jr. in a 1 1/16-mile Keeneland allowance for owners Team Valor International and Gary Barber.
The 7-year-old Ribchester gelding has banked in excess of $5.7 million through a 28-7-7-6 ledger topped by a win in the 2024 Group 1 Dubai Turf. He landed a deep-closing sixth in the Grade 3 Mint Millions on September 7 at Kentucky Downs for his former trainer Jerome Reynier.
“We took him over right after that race. Barry [Irwin] had mentioned to us going into yesterday's race that you need to get him into the race,” Casse said. “We let Irad know you need to be aggressive early on with him and get him into the race and you saw that yesterday. It made the difference. It's a privilege to have that horse in the barn.”
Facteur Cheval will point to the Grade 3 River City on November 7 at Churchill Downs.
Casse enjoyed his second win at the new Belmont Park on Wednesday when Gary Barber’s Ori wired a one-mile turf starter optional-claimer in her first start for new connections after being haltered for $45,000 from an optional-claiming win in September at Saratoga.
With Castellano aboard, the 5-year-old Hard Spun chestnut zipped through splits of 22.39 seconds, 45.09 and 1:09.48 en route to a 6 1/4-length score in 1:33.35. The winning effort returned an 86 Beyer – four points shy of a career-best 90 earned from a runner-up try in the 2024 Listed Winter Memories at Belmont at the Big A.
Ori is out of the stakes-winning Pioneerof the Nile mare Princessof the Nyl. Her stakes-winning third dam, Arabis, is a full-sister to multiple graded stakes-winner Atelier and a half-sister to Grade 1-winner Aldiza.
“We don't claim very many. She's unique in that we thought she looked like she had ability running, but we also claimed her to be a broodmare,” Casse said. “If she keeps running the way she ran the other day, she may run another year.
“Javi called me after the race and said, 'she was impressive.' Normally I call him, but he called me,” Casse added, with a laugh.
Ori will likely point to the Listed $175,000 Noble Damsel, a one-mile turf test for fillies and mares 3-years-old and up on November 27 here.
Casse indicated he will have a big presence in New York this winter for a meet that will be contested exclusively over Tapeta. His significant stock will include a number of horses with past Tapeta experience at Woodbine, whose season comes to a close on December 13.

articles.title_orig: World Wide Technology to Expand Technology Collaboration with Saint Louis University and Become Official Jersey Partner of Billiken Athletics | Newswise
articles.title_zh: World Wide Technology to Expand Technology Collaboration with Saint Louis University and Become Official Jersey Partner of Billiken Athletics | Newswise
articles.content_orig:
New Billikens Athletics Jersey with World Wide Technology Logo
World Wide Technology to Expand Technology Collaboration with Saint Louis University and Become Official Jersey Partner of Billiken Athletics
ST. LOUIS – Saint Louis University (SLU) and World Wide Technology (WWT) announced a strategic partnership that brings together WWT’s expertise in technology, artificial intelligence and data-driven decision-making with SLU’s mission of education, research and community. Combined with a Billiken Athletics sponsorship, this expansion of SLU and WWT’s longstanding partnership will help advance priorities that benefit students, strengthen the University and contribute to the vitality of the St. Louis region.
As part of the agreement, the WWT logo will appear on all team uniforms, making WWT the first official jersey patch partner of Billiken Athletics. WWT will also serve as a strategic advisor and collaborator to accelerate the University's ability to make informed decisions through technology, data and the responsible application of AI.
“World Wide Technology’s journey from a small startup to a global technology leader demonstrates the power of investing in people, ingenuity and purpose,” said Saint Louis University President Edward Feser, Ph.D. “At SLU, we see that potential in our students every day. This partnership reflects the value of mission-driven institutions working together to cultivate talent, advance new ideas, and create opportunities for students and the communities they will serve.”
The new jersey branding will debut during Billiken Athletics games this fall. Highly visible on the court and the field, the branding signifies a deeper relationship between WWT and Billiken Athletics, and a broader collaboration across the University.
The partnership builds on a longstanding relationship between the organizations. Billiken alumni serve in roles across WWT, from technical roles to its leadership ranks, while WWT leaders have served SLU as trustees, advisors and supporters. Through internships, mentoring, philanthropy and engagement with academic and athletic programs, the two organizations have created pathways that connect learning, leadership and career opportunities.
“As an active SLU alumnus and former Billiken soccer team member, I care deeply about supporting the priorities of the University and enriching the student and fan experience,” said Jim Kavanaugh, co-founder and CEO, WWT. “This expanded partnership between SLU and WWT gives the University and its athletics department more capabilities to advance their AI and digital transformation, while growing and developing student athletes.”
WWT and SLU are exploring collaborations that upskill America’s workforce through degree programs and specialized trainings offered by the University’s colleges and Center for Workforce Development. By working together, WWT and SLU can help shape how the latest technologies are deployed to support the missions of higher education and healthcare across the globe.
“Technology decisions at a university impact students, faculty, staff and the community around them,” said Joe Koenig, WWT president SLU alumnus and former Billiken soccer team member. “Through enhanced research capabilities including data analysis, new technology development by faculty and students’ digital experiences, WWT will serve as a strategic advisor for SLU, applying our AI and data expertise to help the University make informed decisions, operate more efficiently and use AI responsibly.”
The partnership makes it possible to bring the benefits of AI to the community, engaging through digital platforms. Fans will have enhanced experiences and data insights will help inform student and athletic programs and reflect community feedback.
“Today’s collegiate athletics landscape requires institutions to think creatively and strategically about how they engage fans, support student-athletes and position their programs for long-term success,” said Chris May, director of athletics at Saint Louis University. “World Wide Technology is a trusted strategic partner whose expertise in building a best-in-class culture and organization has been central to the success of Billiken Athletics. We are thrilled to build on this relationship as we take the next step in our technology strategy and transformation, ultimately enhancing the experience for our Billiken student-athletes and fans.”
About Saint Louis University
Founded in 1818, Saint Louis University is one of the nation’s oldest and most prestigious Catholic research institutions. Rooted in Jesuit values and its pioneering history as the first university west of the Mississippi River, SLU offers more than 12,000 students a rigorous, transformative education that challenges and prepares them for lives of purpose. As a nationally recognized leader in research and innovation, SLU is an R1 research university, advancing groundbreaking, life-changing discoveries that promote the greater good.
About World Wide Technology
World Wide Technology (WWT) is a global technology solutions provider helping organizations make a new world happen by turning ambition into real-world outcomes. Founded in 1990, WWT brings together strategy, deep technical expertise and world-class technology partnerships to help public- and private-sector organizations design, build and scale intelligent AI, digital, cybersecurity, cloud and infrastructure solutions. Through its Advanced Technology Center (ATC), a collaborative ecosystem featuring state-of-the-art hardware and software, WWT enables clients and partners to conceptualize, test and validate innovative technology and then deploy solutions at scale using its global integration and distribution capabilities. With more than 14,000 team members and over 60 locations worldwide, WWT's culture — grounded in core values and leadership philosophies — has been recognized by Fortune and Great Place to Work® for its commitment to innovation, trust and creating a great place to work for all. WWT provides products and services to large enterprises, global service providers and public sector clients in up to 130 countries across six continents. Softchoice, a World Wide Technology company, supports commercial and SMB markets in the U.S. and Canada.

Only Iran and Afghanistan routinely carry out sentences in public, with Saudi Arabia appearing to have ended practice
US politics – live updates
If the US defence secretary, Pete Hegseth, goes ahead with plans to livestream the execution of a soldier radicalised to extremist Islam who killed 13 people at a military base in Texas, his country will join a motley assembly of lesser powers and rogue actors who have conducted public executions in recent years.
Only two countries currently systematically carry out capital sentences in public: Iran and Afghanistan. In 2025, the Taliban authorities carried out six such killings and the regime in Tehran 11, according to Amnesty International .
In April last year, the Taliban executed four men accused of murder in three different cities. All were shot dead in crowded public sports stadiums. Such events were common when the hardline Islamist militia movement was in power in the late 1990s. Then as now, the Taliban claimed a due court process had been followed.
In July, two young men accused of killing police officers were hanged by Iranian authorities in the central square of Isfahan, Iran. Human rights monitors have reported about 30 public executions in Ithe country in the last five years, with an intensification in recent months after massive popular unrest earlier this year and the war with the US and Israel. Historically, many hangings have been carried out using a crane as a makeshift gallows.
Saudi Arabia appears to have ended the practice after decades of beheading convicted criminals in a square in the capital, Riyadh, and sometimes publicly in provincial cities.
Legal experts and historians argue that public executions perform different functions. If the rule of law is shaky or there is doubt about the efficacy of the criminal justice system, they offer authorities seeking to win support a way of convincing the community that criminals will be punished. Such public spectacles can also be a way of cowing a population through terror.
Armed militant groups have frequently resorted to public executions – often in an effort to assert their authority.
Islamic State, which ruled a swath of Iraq and Syria between 2014 and 2019, conducted thousands of executions for alleged offences ranging from homosexuality to theft. Many of the executions took place in public or were videoed. A large number were deliberately choreographed to provide a spectacle for broadcast to terrorise enemies and potential dissidents as well as to radicalise IS supporters and attract new ones.
In October 2025, as Hamas sought to reassert its control over the population of Gaza, it carried out a public execution of six men apparently accused of collaborating with Israel. In 2017, the group had executed three men accused of the same crime, partly livestreaming the event on Facebook .
The execution of Maj Nidal Hasan, a former army psychiatrist, at Fort Hood in Texas would be the first public execution in the US in many decades.
In the US, the practice of public executions was largely stopped in the 1930s, though in 2001, some survivors and victims’ relatives were allowed to watch the execution by lethal injection of Timothy McVeigh, convicted of the 1995 bombing of a government office in Oklahoma City.
Hasan’s execution has been scheduled for 3 December . Hegseth, who has the authority to decide the conduct of the killing, has said that “of course” it would take place at the same time and in the same place as Hasan’s attack 17 years ago and would use firearms, as Hasan did.
Hasan can launch appeals within the civilian federal court system that could delay the execution for many years.
In 2025, Amnesty International recorded 2,707 executions, the highest total globally since 1981, and an increase of two-thirds on the previous year. The sharp rise was mainly due to more than 2,100 executions by Iran , its highest number of executions in decades.
Amnesty said authorities had placed the death penalty “at the centre of flawed public security and ‘tough on crime’ narratives to assert control, project state power and score political points”.
“This trend was strongest in countries where the authorities have tightened their grip on power by restricting civic space, silencing dissent and displaying disregard for protections established under international human rights law and standards,” the campaign group reported.

Jackson County is asking residents to prepare for the Great ShakeOut, the world’s largest earthquake drill scheduled for 10:15 a.m. Thursday, Oct. 15.
Millions of individuals across the globe will practice Drop, Cover and Hold On, the official safety procedure to protect oneself during an earthquake.
This annual event provides an opportunity for people in homes, schools and businesses to assess their disaster preparedness, improve their emergency safety plans and practice what to do in the event of a real earthquake.
For more information and resources to plan your drill, visit shakeout.org/Oregon .
Completing a few small tasks ahead of time, such as assembling a basic emergency supply kit and determining your shelter strategy, helps to assure that you and your family will know what to do and have the supplies you need to be safe wherever you are.
For more preparedness resources and tips, visit ready.gov .
Jackson County will also be conducting a test of the Jackson Alerts notification system in conjunction with the Great ShakeOut.
This service provides critical information quickly for a variety of emergency situations.
To raise awareness and educate the public on disaster preparedness, residents registered with Jackson Alerts will receive a test alert through all listed delivery methods — call, text and email — between 10 a.m. and 2 p.m.
Register, update your Jackson Alerts account and/or find more information at jacksoncountyor.gov/alerts .

articles.title_orig: 'Boy Meets World' star hospitalized after peeing blood
articles.title_zh: 'Boy Meets World' star hospitalized after peeing blood
articles.content_orig:
“Boy Meets World” star Will Friedle is on the mend after a trip to the hospital.
The actor revealed on his “Pod Meets World” podcast with co-stars Rider Strong and Danielle Fishel that he recently “woke up badly peeing blood.”
While the hospital stay was brief, Friedle’s recovery continues.
“Long story short, I'm still in the middle of it. I have a kidney stone,” he explained. “I've got three days of just waiting to see.”
According to Friedle, doctors told him the stone was too small to be broken up with medical intervention.
“Once again, size matters,” he joked, “and above a six is they can do stuff to it, but it's stuff that's apparently very invasive. Where mine's a four—which again I heard is average and most women like.”
Friedle also noted that of all days, his day at the hospital was when fans seemed to recognize him more than ever.
“It gets better,” he said. “Because for some reason, on this day, in that hospital, I was more famous than I've ever been in my life.”
He continued, "One of the nurses comes up to me, and does the Feeny call. She goes, ‘So, here you go, you have a copay, and oh, you want to put it on a credit card?’ I'm like, ‘Yeah, sure.’ Like reach over and I grab and hand her the credit card. And then she looks at me. She goes, ‘Feenay, Fe-hee-nay.’”
“I was like, ‘Thank you so much. Just, just filled up a glass with blood, but thank you,’” he quipped. “‘It's very sweet that you're that you're watching.’”
But Friedle was happy with his care, saying, “They couldn't have been sweeter there. They really couldn't have been nicer.”
And with a little time, Friedle will be fully recovered.
Follow us on Instagram @WeArePauseRewind for all your pop culture obsessions.

articles.title_orig: Real-world data link fezolinetant to fewer nighttime awakenings
articles.title_zh: Real-world data link fezolinetant to fewer nighttime awakenings
articles.content_orig:
Fezolinetant (Veozah) was linked to objective and patient-reported sleep gains in OPTION-VMS, with no new safety signals observed.
Fezolinetant (Veozah) was associated with statistically significant improvements in objective and patient-reported sleep measures among women with bothersome vasomotor symptoms (VMS) in a second preliminary analysis of the ongoing OPTION-VMS study, according to Marla Shapiro, CM, MDCM, CCFP, MHSc, FRCPC, FCFP, MSCP. 1
The prospective, multicenter US study, which was presented at the International Menopause Society 20th World Congress on Menopause, enrolled women aged 40 to 75 years. As of March 2026, 993 users of nonhormonal therapy were enrolled, 859 of whom completed baseline and at least 1 postbaseline assessment. Treatments were grouped by initial prescription: fezolinetant, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs/SNRIs), and other nonhormonal therapies. Sleep was assessed objectively with a medical-grade wearable actigraphy device and subjectively with the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) Sleep Disturbance Short Form 8b at weeks 4, 8, and 12. 1 An earlier preliminary analysis had also reported sleep improvements with fezolinetant. 2
At week 12, fezolinetant was associated with reductions in wakefulness after sleep onset (least squares mean change, −9.45 minutes; 95% CI, −13.93 to −4.96), sleep latency (−1.24 minutes; 95% CI, −1.81 to −0.67), and nighttime awakenings (−2.61; 95% CI, −4.07 to −1.15), as well as increased sleep efficiency (+1.95%; 95% CI, 0.93-2.97) and improved PROMIS total T-scores (−5.69; 95% CI, −6.95 to −4.44) (all P < .001). Improvements were also significant at weeks 4 and 8. 1
Apart from a low-dose SSRI approved in the United States, nonhormonal VMS treatments had historically been used off label, Shapiro noted. The other nonhormonal group consisted primarily of gabapentin, with some pregabalin and clonidine. Results were limited to within-group changes from baseline.
"The study was not designed to compare treatment groups. So they're not head-to-head comparisons," Shapiro said.
SSRIs/SNRIs were not associated with statistically significant improvements in any actigraphy end point. In the other nonhormonal group, the only significant actigraphy improvement was in wakefulness after sleep onset, at weeks 4 and 12. Patient-reported sleep improved significantly in both groups, with PROMIS scores moving from the mild to the no-disturbance range by week 4 with SSRIs/SNRIs and by week 8 with other nonhormonal therapies. 1
No new safety signals emerged. The incidence of drug-related treatment-emergent adverse events, including those leading to drug withdrawal or interruption, was very low with fezolinetant, and no drug-related serious adverse events or hepatotoxicity occurred. 1
"There were 2 cumulative cases of non-serious mild elevated LFTs, neither of which led to treatment or study discontinuation," Shapiro said. Headache and upper respiratory infection were the most commonly reported events, each at a rate of approximately 1.5%.
Findings were consistent across racially and ethnically diverse women, women older than 65 years, women in the menopause transition, and women with obesity. Together with SKYLIGHT trial data from nearly 3000 women and postapproval experience, the findings reinforced a favorable benefit-risk profile for fezolinetant. 3

articles.title_orig: Bose Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar Review: A Great Home Theater Option All By Itself
articles.title_zh: Bose Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar Review: A Great Home Theater Option All By Itself
articles.content_orig:
You won’t feel the need to immediately add a subwoofer to this one.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
When Bose proclaimed that the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar was its "loudest, deepest and most immersive" model yet, I still assumed it would need a subwoofer." Yet when I first connected the company's latest soundbar to my TV, I quickly realized it didn't need the extra bass boost. The combination of CleanBass tech and QuietPort acoustics provide enough low-end tone that you aren't likely to crave an additional, pricey sub. Since the soundbar alone is already $1,099 , that was a welcome surprise.
I get it: There's not a ton of room for innovation when it comes to the design of soundbars. They all have to be elongated and rectangular to be able to contain a collection of drivers without blocking your TV. But there is room for improvement when it comes to the general look of soundbars, and that's where Bose stepped up its game on the Lifestyle Ultra.
The speaker is short and wide, just like you'd expect, but the textured, knit-fabric grille elevates the overall aesthetic. This is more apparent on the white colorway than the black, and luckily the lighter color is exactly what was sent to me for review. Bose also opted for a glass top where the competition typically uses a plastic panel or just buttons. The glass portion doesn't extend all the way to the edges though, so there's room for the up-firing drivers to do their thing.
Another excellent design choice was the volume controls. Bose installed a touch-enabled, circular panel that allows you to spin your finger clockwise and counterclockwise to raise and lower the volume. You can also just tap the "+" or "-" if you'd rather. There's an area in the middle of the circle that you can tap to play, pause or skip tracks, as well as touch-based controls for Bluetooth, disabling the soundbar's microphone and summoning Alexa. All of that is positioned on the right side of the glass panel.
Inside, Bose arranged a collection of nine drivers for the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar's acoustic architecture. There are six full-range drivers, two of which are up-firing and the other four are front facing. Additionally, a center-mounted tweeter assists with dialogue clarity, while two so-called PhaseGuide drivers spread sound horizontally. To calibrate all of that for your living room, Bose's CustomTune feature uses the microphone in your Android or iOS device to analyze the space (speaker layout, surfaces and seating) and optimize the soundbar's output.
Like most soundbars these days, the Lifestyle Ultra only has a single HDMI eARC input. This isn't a problem per se, but if you need HDMI 2.0 passthrough for things like game consoles, just note that it's not available here.
The Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar is very much a plug-and-play device. Once you connect it to power and your TV, it's ready to go. However, you'll want to download the Bose app and run the CustomTune audio calibration ASAP to tailor the soundbar's output to the acoustics of your living room or home theater space. Of course, if you add either the Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer or Lifestyle Ultra Speakers to the soundbar, you'll need to repeat the CustomTune process.
Once all of that is complete, the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar provides a solid boost to your TV audio. The up-firing and PhaseGuide drivers offer a pleasant level of immersion and dimensional audio, which is apparent on shows like Drive to Survive and Masters of the Air. The bass output is the most impressive thing about this soundbar, though. It's enough that users in small to medium spaces likely won't immediately feel the need to add a subwoofer. Even after several weeks of testing, I'm still baffled by the low-end performance when a sound effect demands that portion of the frequency range.
This bass is abundantly apparent for music, too. Sylvan Esso's "Flood Season" has ample lows for the bass guitar riffs and kick drum, while more bass-heavy tracks, like Russian Circles' "Empath," maintain the tonal depth without getting muddy. I also appreciate how the center tweeter allows vocals to consistently float on top of the mix. This makes albums like Hayley Williams' Ego Death At A Bachelorette Party particularly enjoyable.
As I already mentioned, Bose allows you to expand your home theater system with the Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer and Lifestyle Ultra Speakers. Unless you have a larger space, or just crave the extra immersion that rear speakers can provide when watching movies or TV shows, I don't think either are absolutely necessary here.
The speakers are $349 each and the sub comes in at $899, but if you opt for the Home Theater Set or Surround Sound Set (Lifestyle Ultra bundles), you can save a few hundred dollars. (Oddly, Bose doesn't offer savings on the Extra Bass Set, which is the soundbar and subwoofer).
I tested the add-ons one at a time. First, I added the Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer to the soundbar — perhaps the most likely additional purchase for most people. This achieves the obvious result of adding more bass, which could be preferential if you plan for the Lifestyle Ultra gear to pull double duty as your main music setup. But even in my living room, which is open to the main dining area and kitchen, the soundbar alone was still adequate for music.
I then added two Lifestyle Ultra Speakers as rear units, which I quickly discovered would be my preferred way to bolster the soundbar's performance. Since the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar holds its own in the bass department, its only true deficiency is directional audio and overall immersion. Add those two speakers to the rear and that weakness is fixed, and disabling the subwoofer doesn't result in much sacrifice to overall output. I only really noticed a big difference in certain scenes with really booming effects, like certain parts of the first episode of Masters of the Air (no spoilers from me) .
AirPlay, Google Cast and Spotify Connect are all available on the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar for quick and easy music streaming. You can also opt for Bluetooth, if you prefer, but I find the three methods I mentioned are more convenient for getting audio from a phone or laptop to a soundbar.
The Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar does well enough on its own that Bose's primary competition is other companies that claim they've built all-in-one TV speakers that don't need a separate subwoofer. My top pick in that category is Samsung's QS90H , which costs $99 less at full price. This 7.1.2-channel soundbar not only provides adequate bass without a sub, but it has Samsung's Convertible Fit tech that allows you to place it flat or mounted upright. Sensors in the soundbar then reconfigure the output based on how it's sitting. Samsung included lots of other features, but some of them, like Q-Symphony, require a recent Samsung TV to use.
Another excellent option for a true all-in-one soundbar is the Sonos Arc Ultra . The company's flagship model is equipped with Sound Motion technology that handles the bass in a 9.1.4-channel setup. That last number indicates two additional height channels compared to the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar and the QS90H. The Arc Ultra not only has more channels overall, but it also contains more drivers than either the Bose or Samsung options, with 14 of those total. At full price, the Arc Ultra costs the same as the Lifestyle Ultra, but Sonos currently has it on sale for $899 .
Editor's note: Bose is offering a $200 discount on the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar through October 11.
Perhaps Bose's hesitance to label the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar as an all-in-one unit comes down to sales. I'm sure the company would prefer for you to buy the pricey subwoofer for a speaker combo that's common to living rooms. I'd recommend spending extra money on a pair of Lifestyle Ultra Speakers instead, and configure your home theater for better immersion rather than overly booming bass.
No matter what you choose, it won't change the fact that the Lifes
