articles.title_orig: The Brit coaching the world’s game
articles.title_zh: The Brit coaching the world’s game
articles.content_orig:
Central Michigan University soccer head coach James Decosmo looks back at his staff before the game at the Soccer/Lacrosse Complex on Thursday, Sept. 17, 2026. (CM-Life | Jasmine Brookins)
James Decosemo flew from the United Kingdom to the United States more than a decade ago to be a college student, with aspirations of a future in soccer.
Now, he is the head coach of the Central Michigan University women’s soccer team, the sport he has followed his whole life.
“I’m lucky that I get to do it my whole life because it really is my whole life,” Decosemo said.
The James from St. James Park
Decosemo was raised a Newcastle United fan in Stokesley, England and became a season ticket holder at age eight. Even with Newcastle having only won one major trophy in recent history, he fell in love with the sport of soccer because of the Magpies.
In addition to watching legends like Alan Shearer weekly, Decosemo took interest in the manager, Sir Bobby Robson, who also managed Barcelona and the English national team.
“I think he’s a master of man management,” Decosemo said. “I’d love to get to a point where I’m a master of man management.”
Newcastle won its first major competition just a year and a half ago, winning the Carabao Cup 2-1 in 2025 against Liverpool. Decosemo said it is one of the reasons why he loves soccer so much.
“That was an unbelievable moment,” he said. “They hadn’t won one (trophy), obviously in my lifetime, but also in my dad’s lifetime.”
Although his passion ran deep for the Magpies, Decosemo was presented with an opportunity to leave the country to continue to play soccer.
“They introduced us through that process to the opportunity to come to the States to play, which got me really excited,” he said.
The now-Chippewas manager would leave England to go across the pond and into the mitten, attending and playing soccer for Northwood University in Midland, MI.
Since moving to the United States, he’s only been back to St. James Park a handful of times to support Newcastle, but every time has been memorable for Decosemo.
“I went back and watched us play AC Milan in the Champions League, which was awesome,” he said. “If we won, we’d have gone through to the Champions League (knockout stages). If AC Milan win, then they go through ... both teams just going at it.”
Decosemo said that this was the last time he had been back home.
Decosemo met his wife at Northwood. After graduating in 2016, he started his coaching career in Michigan to stay near his wife’s family and the connections he made.
“Probably in all worlds, but soccer especially, there’s a lot of getting jobs through people,” Decosemo said.
Coaching in the US showed him the differences compared to the UK, mainly the rules and the athleticism of the players.
“I think generally, it’s known that the US is more athletic,” he said. “It’s bigger, faster, stronger and the game’s played that way.”
The rule that was so different to him was about substitution. In European soccer, if a player is subbed off, they cannot come back on the pitch later in the game. However, in college soccer, players can come back. The rule changes the pace of the game, ridding the match of lulls, according to Decosemo.
“The game never really changes speed,” he said. “That’s something that definitely I had to adapt to as a player for sure and then as a coach, just knowing that it’s probably a more squad game here than it is other places.”
His first job was at Saginaw Valley State University as a coach for the women’s team, but it wasn’t until his head-coaching job for the women’s team at Aquinas University, that Decosemo was introduced to the difference compared to the men’s game.
“I think the women’s game is probably a little bit more tactical,” he said. “The coach has a little bit more influence in the moment and that’s the way I played and that’s the way I coached.”
Decosemo was the head coach for the Aquinas women’s team from 2022 to 2025. In that span, he recorded a 55-5-7 overall record, with an undefeated 31-0-3 record in the Wolverine Hoosier Athletic Conference. In addition to winning the games, he also won trophies, with five conference championships, with three won in the regular season.
Last year, he made the jump to the NCAA and Division I, going to Kalamazoo to be an assistant coach for Western Michigan’s women’s team. The Broncos went undefeated in the Mid-American Conference, winning both the regular season and post-season competitions, while also beating the Chippewas 3-1.
After the Chippewas let go of their previous head coach last November, Athletic Director Amy Folan called Decosemo about taking the vacant spot a month later.
“When I got the phone call, everything was about trying to win,” he said. “A lot of these jobs, especially in women’s soccer, is just be successful, have a good environment, make sure that the students graduate, which, of course, are important that those things still have to happen here. But the drive to be successful on the field was what I wanted because that’s what I want to do.”
For a manager coming into a new team, it can take a while to adjust the culture and playing style, especially with most of the squad returning. With the team only winning one game last season, the shift was imminent.
“I got to just start with who I am and who we’re going to be rather than maybe navigating to it over a longer period of time,” Decosemo said. “I purposely didn’t ask too much about the previous program and how it was ran. I just went in with what we’re going to do.”
The one collaboration he made with the old program was with assistant coach Keyton Wheelock, who has been at CMU since January 2021.
“We talked a lot about philosophies and the direction he wanted to take the program, and I bought in,” Wheelock said. “I believed in what he was saying and I believed he could make the changes that he said he could make.”
Not only are the returning coaches buying in, the players are also seeing the change.
Rachel Jackson is a senior who earned academic all-conference in 2024 and a team captain in 2025.
“I think we’ve been prepped really well each game knowing what the opponent’s going to do, but always staying true to how we’re going to go with our shape with our attack, with our belief,” Jackson said. “I think we’ve just all been together on the same page from the start of the game to the end of the game.”
Jackson plays a role that is usually referred to as a wingback, where she plays up and down her side of the field. Decosemo said she is the most consistent player on the team and is one of the most impactful.
“The difference probably between Rachel and arguably the rest is that her lows haven’t been noticeable,” Decosemo said. “She’s had some really good moments too, got a game-winning goal in our first win and really contributed in big moments.”
Her game-winning goal was against Charleston Southern University in the second game of the season. Decosemo said the win has been one of his most cherished moments at CMU so far.
“That’s the big standout moment, getting that first win as a group and seeing them celebrate and even hearing the comments say, ‘We don’t know what to do. We’ve won a game,’” he said.
As a manager, the Englishman picks the formation and tactics based on the players on the team. He’s had previous success with the 3-5-2, which also fits the Chippewas’ squad the best. The tactic has three defenders, five midfielders and two strikers. With an overflow of midfielders, the wingers play all over their side of the field.
“The reason that we have wing backs is in my style, our style, the wide players that we have suit that role,” Decosemo said. “They’re physically pretty good at covering ground, but they’re not super crafty or creative in terms of the way they attack, so they’re great at covering, coming from deep and maybe crossing from deep or whatever it is.”
One of the new faces, that has not only surprised Decosemo, but has kept a consistent role in the team, is freshman defender Clai

articles.title_orig: Elon Musk’s growing SpaceX empire sends AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile shares plunging
articles.title_zh: Elon Musk’s growing SpaceX empire sends AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile shares plunging
articles.content_orig:
Elon Musk’s plan for SpaceX to “become a major mobile carrier in the U.S.” sent shares of the nation’s big three wireless carriers sliding by double digits Friday, wiping out more than $50 billion in market value before lunch.
“Once we receive final FCC approval, Starlink Mobile will deploy a flexible architecture combining our satellite-to-mobile constellation in space with an advanced terrestrial deployment that can seamlessly connect devices everywhere,” the company said late Thursday.
It also announced that the Federal Communications Commission had approved the launch of 15,000 new satellites, also under Starlink Mobile, which is a subsidiary of SpaceX.
Shares of AT&T and Verizon both dropped 10% on Friday morning, while T-Mobile US stock plunged 14%.
Shares of Charter and of Comcast, the parent company of NBC News, also fell throughout the day Friday. Both companies sell wireless services under their own brands using Verizon’s infrastructure.
The announcement from SpaceX marked Musk’s latest step to expand his global tech empire. The world’s richest man and its first-ever trillionaire , Musk’s net worth as of Thursday was about $990 billion.
Musk’s constellation of companies already includes electric vehicle maker Tesla, the social media site X and xAI, which builds data centers and develops artificial intelligence.
SpaceX includes multiple lines of business, too. Starlink sells high-speed internet to companies and consumers worldwide, while Starshield does the same, but to governments.
But the major money maker for SpaceX is Starlink, which was worth $2.2 trillion as of Friday.
With more than 12 million paying subscribers, Starlink is also the only profitable part of SpaceX’s business, according to its latest earnings report.
The acquisition of spectrum was “the last critical piece of the spectrum puzzle needed for SpaceX to provide complete phone coverage in America,” Musk wrote on n X.
SpaceX is also a massive U.S. government contractor, building and launching rockets on behalf of NASA and several national security agencies.
Favorable decisions by government regulators and additional agency contracts are crucial to maintaining SpaceX’s lofty valuation.
As a close ally of President Donald Trump and a major donor to his 2024 election effort, Musk is a frequent guest at White House events.
At a recent White House state dinner for China’s President Xi Jinping, Musk was seated next to first lady Melania Trump.
Just this week, Trump gave Musk an award for achievements in science.
As Republicans struggle to hold on to control of the House and Senate in November’s midterm elections, Musk is once again giving tens of millions of dollars to help them.
As of Friday, Musk’s America PAC had spent more than $36 million to boost Trump’s fellow Republicans in key battleground races , according to figures compiled by Wired and verified by NBC News.
Musk also appears to have support for his deal already from FCC chairman Brendan Carr.
“All of this is going to be really good news for the American consumer,” Carr said Friday morning on CNBC .
Wall Street analysts and Starlink’s potential competitors were skeptical Friday of the SpaceX plan.
Absent a deal with an existing wireless carrier, “SpaceX would likely need to build a terrestrial network using macro towers to deliver a user experience on par with traditional wireless carriers,” wrote analysts at JPMorgan Chase.
“We continue to see limited near-term risk to U.S. wireless incumbents given the time, infrastructure and capital required to build a competitive terrestrial network,” they added.
Put another way, the analysts think SpaceX plan’s does not pose an imminent threat to the established carriers because it takes a lot more than just satellites to deliver reliable wireless service.
SpaceX would need earth-based infrastructure to bolster its network of satellites because the radio waves it purchased would likely be unable to reach the interior of some buildings, wrote analysts at UBS. “We still believe it will take time for SpaceX to scale its wireless ambitions.”
Like the analysts, the major telecom companies feeling the sting from Musk’s announcement also downplayed any risk that Starlink might pose to their businesses.
“Acquisition of spectrum alone does not provide the network or infrastructure to offer true nationwide coverage or to compete with mobile providers,” Verizon said in a statement to NBC News. “A company can have billions of dollars of spectrum, but if they do not have the network to use it, it’s just empty airwaves.”
John Saw, president of technology at T-Mobile wrote, “I have tremendous respect for what SpaceX has accomplished in space,” but that building a network would take “years of engineering.”
“You can acquire spectrum in a single transaction. You cannot acquire a nationwide, high-performing wireless network overnight,” he wrote on LinkedIn .
AT&T did not respond to a request for comment on Friday.
The three big wireless companies have a complicated relationship with Starlink. In 2022, T-Mobile announced a partnership with SpaceX, but recently dropped the name of the company from parts of its website.
And when the three wireless companies announced a joint venture recently to “eliminate coverage ‘dead zones’ and expand satellite coverage,” there was no mention of SpaceX or Starlink.

BEIJING — European trade commissioner Maroš Sefčovič said Friday that China has agreed to halve its exports of hybrid cars to the bloc.
Europe has called on China to voluntarily reduce hybrid car exports into the continent, but authorities in Beijing had reportedly slapped down the request , according to the Financial Times.
The widening trade surplus between the EU and China has been a point of contention, with Germany and France previously having called on Brussels to develop a "last-resort" trade instrument to address imbalances.
Sefčovič said Friday that the final decision would still need Brussels' approval. Overall, he cast the two days of talks with China's Commerce Minister Wang Wentao in Beijing as a positive first step, following a summer of rising tensions between China and the EU.
China's Commerce Ministry on Friday released a list of 16 "'consensus outcomes."
They included licenses for rare earth and permanent magnet export licenses to the EU. Sefcovic did not elaborate on a timeline for the rare earth exports.
Earlier this year, on June 29 for the first meeting of the EU-China Trade and Investment Consultations.
The two sides agreed to next meet in March, with a video conference in January, according to the Chinese readout.

President Trump said Russia has agreed to provide the world with millions of tons of diesel fuel over the next several months in a bid to decrease skyrocketing global prices.

Mr. Trump had earlier Friday teased a "big announcement coming up on diesel" during remarks at a Columbus Day celebration.

Mr. Trump pointed out Energy Secretary Chris Wright and said he was "doing a great job."

The Trump administration has looked into several ways to lower diesel prices, most recently signing an executive order this week allowing the use of red-dyed diesel on highways. Red-dyed diesel is exempt from the federal tax of 24.4 cents a gallon that applies to regular diesel.

He said, however, there hasn't been any communication from the U.S. warning of repercussions should Sri Lanka decide to help.
Rodrigo said the ships are stationed 24 nautical miles from Sri Lanka's coast and have reported shortages of food, water and fuel.

The U.K., France, Germany, Australia and Canada have advised their citizens against travel to parts of Saudi Arabia following a wave of Houthi attacks, including one that killed three civilians at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Thursday.

There is currently no warning for U.S. nationals more broadly to avoid Saudi Arabia, but the U.S. embassy in Riyadh urged Americans across the Middle East to "exercise heightened vigilance due to the complex security environment."

articles.title_orig: South African-born jurist Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize for her work in international justice
articles.title_zh: South African-born jurist Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize for her work in international justice
articles.content_orig:
South African judge Navanethem “Navi” Pillay has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, becoming the fifth South African to win it.
Making the announcement on Friday, the Norwegian Nobel Committee praised Pillay for her decades-long efforts to prosecute genocide and war crimes, which have been marked by “judicial rigour, personal integrity and considerable courage”.
From defending activists in apartheid-era South Africa, to more recently overseeing a United Nations inquiry which declared Israel responsible for genocide in Gaza, the 85-year-old, who is also a judge at the International Court of Justice (ICJ), has specialised in international law for decades.
Here’s what we know about her life and why she has been awarded the world’s top peace prize:
Navanethem Pillay, known as Navi Pillay, was born in the racially segregated city of Durban in South Africa’s Natal province in 1940 to parents of Tamil descent.
After earning a law degree from the University of Natal, she became the first woman in Natal province to start her own law firm. Early in her career, she helped defend numerous anti-apartheid activists in the country.
She later became the first woman of colour to sit on the High Court of South Africa. She went on to preside over the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (ICTR), which prosecuted those charged with humanitarian crimes during the 1994 Rwandan genocide .
Pillay was the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) from 2008 to 2014. More recently she chaired the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory which determined last year that Israel is responsible for carrying out genocide in Gaza .
Currently, Pillay is a judge on the International Court of Justice, acting in a case in which Myanmar is accused of genocide against its mostly Muslim Rohingya minority.
Pillay has spent much of her life advocating for human rights in her home South Africa and abroad. While studying, she took part in boycotts and marches against apartheid. She later joined the legal defence of some of the country’s most prominent anti-apartheid figures, such as Phyllis Naidoo and Strini Moodley.
In 1973, Pillay took on a case that helped secure basic rights, including legal access, for political prisoners on Robben Island, where Nelson Mandela was jailed.
In a 2016 interview with the Diplomatic Courier, Pillay said her early human rights work was “shaped by what (she) had experienced under apartheid”.
“I used many of the challenges to my advantage, I had to learn international humanitarian law so as to defend cases of racial discrimination,” she said.
Pillay oversaw a UN commission of inquiry which concluded in 2025 that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza.
In a statement on the report, Pillay urged UN member states to do everything they can to establish a ceasefire in Gaza and to “ensure justice and accountability for all victims”.
The Nobel committee said Pillay was being honoured for her “efforts to promote peace and international law”.
It called her one of “the great defenders of international legal principles in our time”, having helped hold states and national leaders to account and bring “hope to victims of violence and conflict”.
The committee stressed the role Pillay played in the Rwandan genocide tribunal, saying her influence helped establish “that rape and sexual violence could constitute a crime against humanity – as well as genocide”.
“In the same case, Ms Pillay was instrumental in a separate legal breakthrough: for the first time, a defendant faced charges of incitement to commit genocide purely on the basis of spreading propaganda,” said the committee.
The committee said honouring Pillay is especially important at a time when international law “is under tremendous pressure and its institutions are under attack”.
That message was echoed by rights advocates and international officials.
The UN’s rights chief, Volker Turk, said her award was “a recognition, a reaffirmation that human rights, the rule of law and justice and accountability are fundamental to everything, to peace, to security and prosperity”.
International Criminal Court (ICC) President Tomoko Akane said the award carried special significance “at a time of profound challenges to the international legal order and the rule of law”.
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa praised the award as a tribute to Pillay’s “courage, integrity ⁠⁠⁠⁠and lifelong commitment to justice”.
Haakon Gjerlow, acting director of the Peace Research Institute Oslo, said it “sends a clear message that peace depends not only on political leadership, but on strong, credible international institutions and the courageous people who dedicate their lives to defending them .”
Ashok Swain, a professor of peace and conflict research at Uppsala University, told Al Jazeera that the selection of Pillay was a “pleasant surprise” and the “best possible choice”.
He said the Nobel committee likely took into consideration Pillay’s lifelong record fighting genocide and apartheid. He added that the award to the South African jurist could also be read as a message to United States President Donald Trump, who has long argued that he is deserving of the peace prize and whose administration has clashed with South Africa over debunked claims that white Afrikaners are facing “genocide” .
Furthermore, last year, the Trump administration issued sanctions against members of the ICC in what many critics saw as an attack on the system of international law.
The ICC had previously issued arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defence Minister Yoav Gallant for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity.
The ICC responded by describing the US sanctions as a “flagrant attack against the independence of an impartial judicial institution” and the victims of war crimes around the world. It said it would continue its work “without regard to any restriction, pressure or threat”.
Pillay appeared to learn of the award as media reports circulated, telling a group of supporters applauding her: “I don’t know about this. So my question is: Is it true?”
She also jokingly referenced Trump, saying, “If you clap a little bit more, I may share this prize with Trump.”
Once the news was confirmed, Pillay said she would dedicate the award to “all of the survivors of international crimes”.
“This award strengthens my conviction that we must ⁠⁠⁠⁠stand together in defence of ⁠⁠⁠⁠the rule of law, in defence of independent ⁠⁠⁠⁠courts and an international ⁠⁠⁠⁠legal order based ⁠⁠⁠⁠on principle.”
Earlier, the Nobel committee said it had struggled to get in touch with Pillay to notify her. “If you see a Norwegian number calling, please pick up,” said committee chair, Jorgen Watne Frydnes.

articles.title_orig: Trump establishes committee to investigate Federal Reserve's Lisa Cook in latest effort to fire her
articles.title_zh: Trump establishes committee to investigate Federal Reserve's Lisa Cook in latest effort to fire her
articles.content_orig:
BREAKING: Trump eases Russia sanctions to allow Putin to release diesel fuel onto the global market amid price spike
President Donald Trump on Friday signed an order directing the attorney general and other top federal officials to establish a committee to investigate Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook, in his latest attempt to fire her.
“By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, I hereby establish a committee of inquiry (Committee) to investigate allegations that Federal Reserve Governor Lisa D. Cook made false statements in connection with one or more mortgage instruments,” read a presidential memorandum posted to the White House website.
It said that the committee would “investigate the allegations against Governor Cook and report to me whether there is ‘cause’ for Governor Cook’s removal.”
“Governor Cook may submit a written position statement to the Committee regarding the allegations,” the memorandum said.
The unprecedented White House announcement comes after a top White House official in August wrote a letter to Cook , saying that Trump was considering removing her from the Federal Reserve board.
The White House memorandum said that Cook “shall appear at the hearing and be examined by the Committee,” as well as “present argument, written evidence, and written witness statements regarding the evidence and allegations.”
The committee is set to meet Nov. 5 for the hearing, two days after the midterm elections. No president has ever fired a top Fed official.
“In light of the President’s repeated statements that he has already decided to fire Governor Cook — regardless of the facts and evidence —  we have grave doubts that this ‘hearing’ is a legitimate one that would conform to the law,” said Abbe Lowell and Norm Eisen, Cook’s attorneys.
“But if it is anything close to objective, the conclusion will be that Governor Cook did not commit mortgage fraud, leaving no cause to remove her from the Federal Reserve Board.”
Lowell and Eisen said they have engaged with the White House to determine if this is a “genuine” process and that Cook “welcomes the opportunity to present the facts so she can clear her name and demonstrate there is no legal basis to fire her.”
The memo follows a Supreme Court ruling in June, which allowed Cook to remain in her job for now. But the justices did not permanently block Trump from removing Cook, instead ruling that she had the right to an opportunity to defend herself.
Trump’s latest move stems from allegations first leveled against Cook in August 2025 by Federal Housing Finance Agency chief Bill Pulte. Trump amplified those allegations on social media and, citing a “criminal referral” he said Pulte had sent to the Justice Department, attempted to remove her from the Fed’s board.
Pulte alleged that Cook committed mortgage fraud, however documents obtained and reviewed by NBC News later revealed that Cook declared that the property in question was to be used as a “vacation home” and not her primary residence.
The Federal Reserve declined to comment on Friday’s developments.
Other top Trump administration officials, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, reportedly have similar mortgage situations.
Former Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin have all called more than one property their “primary residence” on mortgage applications, according to a report last year from ProPublica .
Cook, a governor on the Federal Reserve’s board, has a permanent vote on interest rates. Trump and Pulte’s attacks on Cook came amid a long-running pressure campaign by the administration to get the U.S. central bank to cut interest rates.
“President Trump is convening an illegitimate show trial in his dangerous quest to illegally take over our nation’s central bank,” said Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee, which oversees the Fed.
“Instead of playing judge in a kangaroo court of his own making, Trump should end the war in Iran and cancel his chaotic tariffs,” Warren said.
Trump also recently resumed his attacks on another Fed governor, Jerome Powell. Trump claimed Sept. 30 that the former chairman was complicit in cost overruns for a construction project at the central bank’s headquarters. However, an inspector general’s report found no wrongdoing.
Trump responded to the report by writing on social media, “He should be forced to resign, IMMEDIATELY! If he doesn’t resign, he should be sued, at the highest level, by the United States Government, for either corruption or incompetence.”
Following the post, Attorney General Todd Blanche told Bloomberg News , “We’re not reopening a criminal investigation into him.”
Powell has remained on the Fed’s board despite the end of his term as chair, breaking with tradition. As long as Powell remains on the board, the Trump administration is denied the opportunity to name a new board member of the president’s choice.
Cook has consistently maintained that she did nothing wrong.
Just weeks ago, Cook’s lawyer told the White House for a second time that, “There is no legal basis for President Trump to remove Governor Cook for cause.”
“An inadvertent error is not fraud, as the President and a third of his cabinet should know because they reportedly did the same thing,” Abbe Lowell said Aug. 26. “These attacks on Governor Cook are not about real estate paperwork; they are an attempt by President Trump to force the Federal Reserve to bend to his will.”
Lowell said he and Cook were prepared to continue to fight “any illegal attempt to remove Governor Cook.”
Steve Kopack is a senior reporter at NBC News covering business and the economy.

articles.title_orig: Ex-German Chancellor Schröder attends Putin's birthday bash
articles.title_zh: Ex-German Chancellor Schröder attends Putin's birthday bash
articles.content_orig:
Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder attended Russian President Vladimir Putin 's birthday party, the Kremlin said Thursday.
Putin celebrated his 74th birthday in Moscow on Wednesday. The Kremlin said Putin learned that Schröder was on a business trip in the Russian capital via Russian media reports.
"The president invited his old friend to his home," the Kremlin said, with the Russian government releasing pictures of Schröder and Putin smiling and clasping hands.
Schröder , who is 82 years old, was in Moscow visiting one of the branches of the new Hyperglobus supermarket chain. The ex-German chancellor was named to the chain's supervisory board last week.
Hyperglobus was originally part of German retail company Globus Holding, which operates the Globus supermarkets in Germany and the Czech Republic.
Globus Holding also had supermarkets in Russia, but divested its stake last year, with those stores thus being spun off into separate company Hyperglobus.
Schröder, a member of the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) , served as Germany's chancellor from 1998 to 2005.
Since leaving the chancellery, Schröder has worked for Russian state-owned energy firms and has also maintained personal contact with Putin.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Schröder's fondness for Russia has drawn controversy, particularly since the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Schröder's tax-payer financed Berlin office was closed in 2022 over his involvement in the Russian energy sector, and he has also faced calls by fellow party members to be expelled from the SPD.
Schröder, however, has survived the attempt to be kicked out of his party.

articles.title_orig: Europe’s Car Lobby Says EU-China Deal Can Ease Chinese Hybrid Surge ‘in Orderly Way’
articles.title_zh: Europe’s Car Lobby Says EU-China Deal Can Ease Chinese Hybrid Surge ‘in Orderly Way’
articles.content_orig:
Brussels says Beijing’s shipments could fall by more than half over four years, cutting millions of vehicles amid fears for European jobs
The EU said it has reached a landmark deal with China to “halve” its sales of hybrid cars in the bloc amid fears surging sales could kill off parts of the European car industry.
Trade commissioner Maroš Šefčovič said the deal was the first of its kind and the result of “intense” negotiations with China since June to curb a trade deficit of €1.18bn (£1bn) a day, which has caused mounting tensions between the two economic powers.
The deal “opens the prospect of cutting China’s export [of hybrids] by more than a half”, Šefčovič said, adding that this would translate into a reduction in exports of plug-in and battery-powered hybrid cars by “several millions” over the next four years, said Šefčovič said Šefčovič at a press conference in Beijing on Friday.
“It is the first time that China has accepted to moderate its exports without going through the phase of prior trade tension,” he said, a reference to the usual investigations that must take place before safeguards under WTO trading rules are put in place.
China has been flooding Europe with cars , including hybrids and pure battery electric vehicles (BEVs), threatening European manufacturers. Hybrids combine an internal combustion engine with a small battery. They are sold by carmakers as a transitional step towards BEVs.
Šefčovič said the Chinese had recognised the political pressure building in every member state in Europe with “literally thousands of job losses” at risk because of the flood of cheap imports from China across many sectors including chemicals and textiles.
He said EU leaders were “clearly expecting very fast action” from the European Commission and the Chinese recognised that.
“I am glad to say that the Chinese partners appreciated this very strong political argument, and therefore, we can proceed through the negotiated solution,” he said.
“This ‌is far from the end. It’s a crucial first step, but only a first step,” Šefčovič told ‌reporters in Beijing where he had travelled to hold ​talks with his Chinese counterpart.
Earlier this week senior EU officials said they were heading to Beijing to seek what they called a “proof of concept” or pilot scheme with one sector which they hoped could then be expanded to other areas under pressure from Chinese competition.
Šefčovič said he put “so much emphasis” on the negotiations because it was “very difficult to stop” a trade war once it was declared.
As part of a 16-point agreement, Beijing and Brussels will continue negotiating on cars, export restrictions on rare earths and access to China for more food and drink from the EU.
after newsletter promotion
China said both sides would adhere to “procedures concerning company price undertakings” for hybrid cars suggesting one method of curbing sales would be to set higher minimum price tags for Chinese cars sold in Europe.
The EU commissioner will brief EU diplomats in Brussels on Sunday ahead of a leaders’ summit on Thursday.
A statement from the Chinese ministry of commerce said China is “willing … to continue facilitating the approval of export licenses for rare earths and permanent magnets destined for the EU”.
It added that both sides had “reaffirmed their commitment … to properly handle differences within the framework of WTO rules, and to continuing to stabilise and balance bilateral trade and economic relations”.
While China and the EU acknowledged “differences” between them it appears that China has accepted the EU’s request to create a new model for trade balances starting with a pilot on hybrid cars.

articles.title_orig: US diesel prices remain high despite Trump's moves to boost supplies
articles.title_zh: US diesel prices remain high despite Trump's moves to boost supplies
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
By Jarrett Renshaw and Nicole Jao
WASHINGTON/NEW YORK, Oct 9 (Reuters) - US diesel prices remain at near-record highs, up 70% since the US-Israeli war on Iran began despite two recent moves by President Donald Trump to boost supplies: pressuring allies to release emergency reserves and ‌expanding access to tax-exempt red-dyed diesel.
The wars in Iran and Ukraine have triggered a severe global fuel supply crunch, pushing the average ‌US diesel price to $6.28 a gallon on Friday, according to motorist group AAA.
"Aside from a recession that hammers consumption, the only thing that can prevent oil prices from rising further and ​put them on a sharp downward trajectory is a durable end to conflicts in the Arabian Gulf and between Russia and Ukraine," said Bob McNally, president of Rapidan Energy Group. "Otherwise, policy options range from marginal to counterproductive."
High fuel prices have made it harder for Trump and his Republican Party to defend narrow congressional majorities in the November 3 midterm elections. The cost of living is the top item cited by voters in a Reuters/Ipsos poll, and high diesel prices put particular ‌pressure on traditional Republican constituencies: farmers, truckers and rural ⁠voters.
Trump's approval rating is at a career-low 32%, according to the poll.
The administration has touted a G7 agreement to release 100 million barrels of oil and petroleum products as a major step to help ease prices, but those barrels ⁠appear to largely cover what remains of a March emergency release by International Energy Agency members, rather than new supply.
A White House official disputed that characterization, saying the earlier commitments were not specifically for refined products. The administration negotiated for the previously committed barrels to be front-loaded with diesel and released on a tight timeline beginning ​immediately, ​the official said.
The White House said Trump was focused on easing temporary disruptions while pursuing ​longer-term energy policies.
The administration's other major initiative, an executive ‌order allowing red-dyed diesel on public roads through year-end, has drawn limited industry uptake. The fuel is chemically identical to what trucks normally burn but is tinted to show it is exempt from the 24.4-cent-per-gallon federal highway tax.
The order defers the federal tax and waives penalties for burning off-road fuel on highways. But major retailers and marketers remain wary of selling it because of unclear tax liabilities, logistical hurdles and the risk of fines when trucks cross state lines.
The tax savings are relatively small with diesel prices above $6 a gallon.
David Fialkov, who lobbies on behalf of NATSO, a trade group for truck stops ‌and travel centers, said the White House appeared to be encouraging the supply chain to ​sell dyed fuel through channels not traditionally used for highway diesel, but said that most ​reputable retailers and marketers were unlikely to do so.
John Tirado, president ​of New Jersey-based commercial fuel supplier Summa Energy, called the red-dyed diesel plan "a Band-Aid on a much bigger problem."
The White ‌House said more than 4,000 retailers distribute dyed diesel. It ​said Treasury Department guidance will clarify the ​rules, allowing drivers to use it without federal tax or penalty. It said the savings should outweigh any detour costs for truckers seeking the fuel.
"The fundamental problem facing the US is not taxation but an exceptionally tight global market for refined products," said Caspian Conran, lead economist ​at Baringa, citing disruptions to energy flows from the ‌Middle East and reduced refining output elsewhere.
He described the measures as short-term steps ahead of the election that could provide "probably a few ​weeks of relief," rather than a durable solution.
(Reporting By Jarrett Renshaw in Washington, Additional reporting by Nicole Jao in New York ​and Timothy Gardner in Washington; Editing by Nathan Crooks, David Gregorio, Rod Nickel)

articles.title_orig: One World Community Health Center hosts free health fair in Omaha
articles.title_zh: One World Community Health Center hosts free health fair in Omaha
articles.content_orig:
By Hannah Nazarenus , News intern
Oct. 9, 2026, 10:48 a.m. ·
One World Community Health Center will host a free, family-friendly health fair Saturday at the South Omaha Campus of Metropolitan Community College as part of Binational Health Week.
The event is open to anyone, regardless of insurance status or whether they are a One World patient, said Vivian Garcia, outreach manager at One World. The fair runs 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.
“Right now, we can see that there's a lot of families that are struggling to even cover that extra cost that insurance doesn't cover,” Garcia said. “So that’s the reason why we invite everyone. It doesn't matter if you have health insurance, if you don't have health insurance.”
Garcia said they expect more than 400 people, up from last year, when attendance was still recovering after COVID-19 forced the events to pause.
“It’s not about getting more patients for a clinic,” Garcia said. “It’s about getting these resources and getting education out in a community.”
Visitors can get cholesterol, blood sugar and blood pressure checks. Specialty services include dermatology, hearing and vision screenings, and basic dental screenings for adults and children. This will be the first year the fair offers ear cleanings for people who fail the hearing test.
Vision services have drawn the most interest, Garcia said. This is the second year the fair will offer full vision screenings with glasses prescribed on site.
“The only thing that they're going to be asked is a good address to have those glasses sent over to their home,” Garcia said.
More than 200 people received glasses that way last year.
Garcia said the fair connects attendees to One World and other clinics and organizations in the Omaha area. Participants fill out a short form with no identifying information.
“What we also hear a lot is just navigating the healthcare system overall,” Garcia said. “Knowing how to go into a provider, to the clinic, to set up an initial appointment. Sometimes individuals are maybe just arriving here in Nebraska, and they don't know exactly where to go.”
Binational Health Week is an initiative of the Mexican government, and One World coordinates its events with the Mexican consulate.
The Saturday fair is the last of three October events. One World also held one Oct. 3 at All Care Health Center in Council Bluffs, Iowa, and a women’s night offering breast exams and cancer screenings in partnership with UNMC.
More information on the event and others hosted by One World can be found on its website.

Moderna ( MRNA ) stock popped 9% on Friday after the New York Times reported new details about an effort to accelerate cancer vaccine development. Investors saw the mRNA biotech company, in particular, as a beneficiary.
Other pharmaceutical stocks, including Pfizer ( PFE ), BioNTech ( BNTX ), and Merck ( MRK ), also rose.
According to the New York Times, the new initiative is a public-private partnership — similar to the effort that produced COVID-19 vaccines — that involves the National Institutes of Health (NIH), the NIH's nonprofit arm, researchers, pharmaceutical and biotech companies, advocacy groups, other nonprofits, and patients.
Stacey Adam, a senior clinical officer at the NIH's foundation, told the New York Times that she expects the program to launch in December. In 2024, the UK launched a similar program, called the Cancer Vaccine Launch Pad .
Moderna is viewed as a leader in mRNA cancer treatments. The stock soared in August on positive results for a melanoma treatment , developed with Merck.
Year to date, Moderna stock is up 627%.

articles.title_orig: China and Europe Step Back From Trade War With Limits on Chinese Car Exports
articles.title_zh: China and Europe Step Back From Trade War With Limits on Chinese Car Exports
articles.content_orig:
The agreement will see Chinese hybrid vehicle exports decline by ‘several million cars’ in the coming years, EU trade chief says
The European Union and China have “reached an understanding” that will cut Chinese hybrid car shipments to the bloc by “more than a half”, in a temporary salve to trade tensions that have threatened to boil over into a full-blown trade war.
Speaking after marathon trade talks in Beijing, EU trade chief Maros Sefcovic said the deal would see China slash its hybrid car exports “by several million cars” over a four-year period.
“This is the first time that China has accepted to moderate its exports without going through the phase of prior trade tensions, and I very much appreciate that,” Sefcovic told reporters in the Chinese capital.
The sides also agreed to expedite EU applications for rare earth mineral export licences and improve market access for goods including car parts, olive oil and textiles, which Sefcovic said could be worth “almost €4 billion” (US$4.5 billion) in current export value.

articles.title_orig: Get in the Spotlight With the Line Life Podcast
articles.title_zh: Get in the Spotlight With the Line Life Podcast
articles.content_orig:
A few years ago, I partnered with Danielle Blanchette and our team from T&D World to launch the  Line Life Podcast. Our mission was simple: to bring the stories from the pages of T&D World magazine to the airwaves.
Due to the nature of their jobs, lineworkers are not in an office working behind a computer day in and day out. Instead, they are slipping on their work boots, packing their tool bags and heading out in the field to keep the power flowing to the customers in their service territories.
Because lineworkers spend a lot of time traveling from one location to the next in their bucket trucks, we wanted to give them a way to listen to our field-focused Electric Utility Operations (EUO) stories on the go.
We started with only audio stories, and then we started branching out into interview-style episodes. For the last few years, I've recorded interviews with lineworkers and their loved ones for future episodes of the Line Life Podcast.
With the 2026 International Lineman's Rodeo Week only a few days away, we're excited to offer that opportunity again to the Lineman's Rodeo attendees. Swing by the T&D World Booth #001 (in the breezeway between the ballroom and the exhibit hall) to sit down with me, Amy Fischbach, for a conversation about your career in the line trade.
I air interview-style episodes on the first and third Fridays of each month and audio stories on the second and fourth Fridays on Podbean and in your favorite podcasting app.
To see all the episodes we've recorded over the years, go to linelife.podbean.com . You can also check out our new International Lineman's Rodeo Roundup page on our T&D World website to see the past Rodeo-related episodes.
I look forward to seeing you during the 2026 International Lineman's Rodeo and putting you in the spotlight for the Line Life Podcast!
Amy Fischbach is the Head of Content for T&D World magazine and manages the Electric Utility Operations section. She is the host of the Line Life Podcast , which celebrates the grit, courage and inspirational teamwork of the line trade.  She also works on the annual Lineworker Supplement and the Vegetation Management Supplement as well as the Lineman Life and Lineman's Rodeo News enewsletters. Amy also covers events such as the Trees & Utilities conference and the International Lineman's Rodeo. She is the past president of the ASBPE Educational Foundation and ASBPE and earned her bachelor's and master's degrees in journalism from Kansas State University. articles.title_orig: Apple ‘Welcome home’ event: Three new products are coming next week
articles.title_zh: Apple ‘Welcome home’ event: Three new products are coming next week
articles.content_orig:
Apple officially confirmed yesterday that it will hold a product launch event next week on October 13. With a “Welcome home” tagline, the launch is expected to focus on new smart home products. Here’s everything to expect at next week’s Apple event.
9to5Mac’s Apple event coverage is supported by Sony : Shop Sony’s huge Amazon sale to score big savings on its entire TV lineup, including models with Apple AirPlay 2 support.
There are two components to the event, as Ryan outlined . There is the in-person experience for members of the press in New York City, as well as what Mark Gurman has called an “online video presentation.”
This suggests we can expect press releases and a video (or videos) to drop around 9 a.m. ET/6 a.m. PT on October 13. Apple hasn’t confirmed this, so the actual launch might vary. At a minimum, though, we know it will announce something on October 13, and some people will see it in person while the rest of us follow along from home.
Next week’s headlining announcement will be Apple’s long-rumored smart display product, which we’ve been calling the “HomePad.” Apple believes that this product can serve as a central hub for your house, powered by Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.
According to Bloomberg , the device will have a 6-inch square display atop a half-dome base, with a metal arm holding it up. The HomePad will reportedly come in two variations: one that can be mounted on a wall and one that can sit on a countertop. Reports have likened the design to Apple’s iconic iMac G4 .
One of the flagship features of the HomePad will be its ability to recognize multiple people in a household. Mark Gurman reports that it can recognize who is talking to it or approaching it and dynamically adjust what’s shown on the screen.
In terms of software , the HomePad reportedly mixes different elements of the Apple Watch, Apple TV, and iPad. This includes iPad-like app designs and Apple Watch-style icons. It will also heavily borrow from the iPhone for widgets and StandBy mode .
Apple is also expected to announce a new Apple TV 4K next week, its first update to the set-top box since November 2022. The new Apple TV will look the same as its predecessor, but it will reportedly include the A19 or A19 Pro chip.
That upgraded chip will allow Apple to bring Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features to the Apple TV for the first time.
Apple is also reportedly working on new software features for the Apple TV and HomePod. For example, there are code references to a new feature that would let you arrange four full-sized HomePods in a surround sound system when paired with Apple TV.
The HomePod mini will also get its first proper upgrade next week. The big change here will be a new chip that is much faster than the current model’s S5 processor, bringing support for Siri AI. For context, the S5 chip used in the current HomePod mini is the same chip Apple debuted with the Apple Watch Series 5.
Beyond the faster chip, the new HomePod mini 2 will reportedly come in new colors:
Finally, Apple is working with LG on new “second-party” accessories for HomeKit. Apple reportedly collaborated with LG to co-develop products including a smart lock, thermostat, doorbell, and multiple cameras.
Bloomberg says Apple won’t release these accessories for “at least a few more months.” They could still be shown off as part of Apple’s broader home strategy next week, though.
While we obviously have a pretty good idea of what Apple will announce next week thanks to these rumors, I’m still really excited to see the company unveil its home roadmap. It’s felt like a category Apple has neglected for far too long, and one it might finally start taking seriously next week.
What are you most excited to see at Apple’s “Welcome home” event next week? Are you planning to buy the all-new HomePad or upgrade your Apple TV and HomePod mini? Let us know down in the comments.

articles.title_orig: Hack the World: Why hackathons are still the best place to learn to build
articles.title_zh: Hack the World: Why hackathons are still the best place to learn to build
articles.content_orig:
Someone bursts through the door and announces, “There’s pizza!” Nearby, a team has duct tape and cardboard holding its prototype together. Another is debugging a model that won’t detect their movements.
This is a common scene during hackathons, and for a lot of people they’re the place to learn to build.
During several recent hackathons, we followed dozens of participants from the badge line to final demos and asked them what keeps them coming back.
Teams come up with ideas for robots, apps, websites, hardware, and more, then try to get prototypes working before time runs out.
These aren’t small things, these are big endeavors, and they’re going to try to do it in basically two days.
Yana describes it as two days of intense focus on one small experimental project that moves the needle forward. For Nithya, it’s a rare chance to work as hard as you can on something you’re proud of.
It is basically an invention marathon.
For most of computing history, building software required years of specialized training. Not anymore: with AI-powered tools like GitHub Copilot, natural language is becoming a universal programming language, and anyone with an idea can start turning it into working code.
Lance’s team hit a problem at the very last minute. They needed a news API so people could fact-check the information they were getting.
GitHub Copilot was able to not only create a frontend in 30 minutes but also connects with the actual API itself and integrates it all together.
When they’re paired up with someone that’s a CS major, or when they just go and use AI to start a prototype and convince others to join in on their idea, it’s giving this autonomy for people to do what they’re most passionate about.
Call it a learning event, Jon says, and people might not want to go. But tell them there’s pizza, and they’ll show up anyway, and they’ll still end up learning.
Jon calls it the best educational experience you can get as a technologist. Sarvesh puts it more simply: it’s a better way to learn.
Eric calls hackathons a huge grind of continuous work and continuous debugging. Vaishnavi’s team spent part of the time fighting a model that couldn’t detect their movements. “Like, nothing is working,” Vaishnavi said at one point. Mayank’s team got there through trial and error, with duct tape and cardboard.
Hackathons are a safe third place. It’s okay to fail and experiment. You’re not going to get an F, you’re not going to get fired over it.
Niels once searched Google to find out who came up with the term “hackathon,” and his own name came up. He doesn’t remember coining it, but he does remember setting laptops down wherever there was space, sleeping on the floor in sleeping bags, and going straight back to hacking after waking up.
If you feel you have to do it and you don’t like the people around you, then you’re missing the point.
Akankshya found everyone open to collaborating and never felt pushed to quit or leave. Shehmeer could turn to the person on either side and ask how to do something. If they didn’t know, they usually knew someone there who did.
My first hackathon, I met two guys that are now my best friends.
When you meet someone who you bond with over a shared interest, that’s a friendship of practice.
Mike’s first hackathon changed the course of his career:
At my first hackathon, I learned more in one weekend than I had in my entire university degree up to that point.
The next day, Mike looked in the mirror and told himself to forget being a lawyer and become a hacker.
Lee has seen hackathons act as a bridge between the spark of an idea and something rolled out into production. Shehmeer says organizers are trying to show a new generation that building isn’t out of reach.
For Yana, seeing the work happen pulls more people in, because there’s now a bit more of an open door.
You can solve problems yourself, you don’t have to ask someone else for permission.
Everyone is welcome. Student or professional. All identities. All abilities. All backgrounds. All experience levels.

articles.title_orig: Is China Derailing Its Own Recovery?
articles.title_zh: Is China Derailing Its Own Recovery?
articles.content_orig:
China wants to revive its economy, but its policy choices keep getting in the way. Is Beijing self-sabotaging its own recovery? Benzinga contributor Doug Young of Bamboo Works weighs in:
The country needs to take stronger, more decisive steps, place greater value on its consumers and rein in its frequent crackdowns to jumpstart the economy
China wants to right its economy ship, which has slowed sharply in the last few years after more than two decades of breakneck growth that made it the world’s second-largest economy. The only problem is, the country can’t seem to shake its old tendency to crack down on sectors it sees as challenging the social and economic order.
What’s more, it is only giving limited help to consumers who have the power to perk up the economy with their spending. Again, this looks like inability to shake its past tendency to treat such consumers as a second thought, as the government put all its focus on the very economic development that’s now sputtering.
Underpinning the current economic malaise is a Chinese property market that has been slumping for the last five years, following two decades that saw prices post manyfold meteoric gains. Most home prices are now at least 40% below their peaks, sometimes much more in smaller markets where supply far exceeds demand.
As prices slump, Chinese, who often see real estate as their primary savings vehicle, are seeing their individual wealth dry up in tandem. Property accounted for 52% of household assets at the start of this year, down sharply from 67% in mid-2021 when prices were near their peak, according to data cited in a South China Morning Post report.
China has taken repeated steps to try to perk up the market, most recently rolling out a new nationwide mortgage-interest subsidy for first-time home buyers last month. Yet at the same time, it continues to punish the home developers that are struggling under huge debt incurred during a building spree that left the market vastly oversupplied.
Downfall of a property titan
In the most recent move that won’t bring much confidence back to the market, a court in August sentenced Hui Ka Yuan, founder of Evergrande , poster child for the industry’s excesses, to life in prison for a range of financial crimes. At the same time, it also formally started to liquidate his company in bankruptcy court. While that ended five years of uncertainty about the company, it hardly sent a positive signal to the many other developers out there still trying to work through their debt problems.
The property sector is far from the only one being subjected to the type of government crackdown that used to be relatively common in China but had become less so in recent years.
Another prominent crackdown began earlier this year when the government launched an anti-trust probe against leading online travel agent Trip.com (TCOM.US; 9961.HK) that ultimately resulted in a massive 5.2 billion yuan ($776 million) in fines and other penalties. But the market regulator didn’t stop there, and is now conducting similar investigations against smaller but still sizable online travel agents including Tongcheng (0780.HK), as well as services run by Alibaba (BABA.US; 9988.HK) and Meituan (3690.HK).
In another similar crackdown, the city of Beijing suddenly rolled out a massive no-fly zone for smaller aircraft over the city last month after one such aircraft crashed into the city’s tallest building in June. While such moves may protect China’s cities from similar accidents, they are also almost certain to cast a chill over companies like EHang (EH.US), a maker of tourism-use small aircraft, that Beijing had been fostering to help build the country’s low-altitude economy.
The government is also taking similar steps to tamp down overheated competition that resulted in massive excess capacity in the solar and wind equipment sectors, as well as in new energy vehicles (NEVs). A rapid buildup of those sectors, with strong government support, helped to fuel China’s economic growth in the go-go days. But now such government-led attempts to correct the problem are only exacerbating the current economic slowdown.
Then there’s China’s massive base of 1.4 billion consumers, whose collective spending power could help revive the economy. This group was traditionally overlooked by China, which preferred to rely on exports, foreign investment and infrastructure spending to power its economic miracle.
Now, the government is finally turning its attention to this potential source for jumpstarting the economy. But many of its efforts feel like too little too late, and are often half-hearted. Weak job and property markets aren’t helping either, since uncertainties over home values and job prospects are leading many consumers to cut back on their spending, especially for items seen as non-essential like travel and restaurant dining.
China has publicized a number of programs aimed at pumping up consumer spending. The highest profile of those was a trade-in program that provided government subsidies for people who traded in old items like home appliances and electronics for new ones. But that program, originally launched in 2024 and which the government says supported sales worth 2.61 trillion yuan in 2025, is rapidly losing momentum this year as most people have run out of things to trade in.
Incentives that helped to charge up China’s NEV sales are also being pared back as the government tries to force the industry to stand on its own, even as most companies are still losing money. A program that exempted NEVs from China’s vehicle purchase tax ended at the end of last year, replaced by one that only exempted them from half of the tax this year. That caused purchases to spike at the end of last year, only to slow sharply this year.
As that happened, many individual NEV makers have reported their domestic sales slid into reverse this year. And while many are trying to sell more abroad to keep their sales growing, the resulting huge flood of exports has only raised alarm bells among many of China’s major trading partners.
Many have argued that China needs to take bolder steps to jumpstart its economy compared with the smaller incremental ones it has taken so far. It also needs to shake some of its old habits, such as regular crackdowns on emerging industries, and do more to encourage its 1.4 billion consumers to relax their fondness for saving and spend more on enjoying their country’s newfound prosperity.

articles.title_orig: EU takes 'crucial first step' toward rebalancing trade with China: Trade commissioner
articles.title_zh: EU takes 'crucial first step' toward rebalancing trade with China: Trade commissioner
articles.content_orig:
The EU has taken a "crucial first step" toward rebalancing trade relations with China after reaching an understanding on hybrid vehicle exports, EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic said Friday.
Speaking at a news conference in Beijing, Sefcovic said the understanding could pave the way for reducing Chinese exports of hybrid and plug-in hybrid vehicles to the European market by more than half.
"This opens the prospect of cutting China's export by more than a half," he said, describing the understanding as the first tangible outcome of trade and investment consultations between Brussels and Beijing.
Sefcovic said the EU had sought to rebalance trade relations with China amid a growing trade deficit and concerns over global industrial overcapacity.
He said the understanding was particularly important for Europe's automotive industry, which was under significant pressure.
The negotiated solution was fair and consistent with World Trade Organization methodology, he added.
"For the first time that China has accepted to moderate its export without going through the phase of prior trade tension," Sefcovic said, welcoming the outcome of the negotiations.
He said the understanding covered seven specific tariff lines and could reduce Chinese exports of hybrid and plug-in hybrid vehicles to the EU by several million cars over four years.
Sefcovic added that the EU would proceed with the relevant procedures once the understanding received endorsement from the bloc's leaders.
"This is far from the end. It's a crucial first step, but only a first step in the process of rebalancing," he said.
Trade between China and the EU remains heavily weighted in Beijing's favor.
According to European Commission data, the bloc imported approximately $650 billion worth of goods from China in 2025, compared with exports of $232 billion, leaving a merchandise trade deficit of around $418 billion.
Machinery and vehicles accounted for more than half of manufactured imports from China, according to the data.
The imbalance has become a central concern in Brussels, which has urged Beijing to open its market further to European companies and address what it describes as unfair competition and industrial overcapacity.
The two sides agreed to hold their next ministerial-level meeting in March 2027, preceded by a video conference in January.

articles.title_orig: U.S. measles cases top 4,000, far surpassing last year's total, CDC says
articles.title_zh: U.S. measles cases top 4,000, far surpassing last year's total, CDC says
articles.content_orig:
The record number of measles cases in the U.S. so far this year has topped 4,000, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported Friday.
The agency said there were 4,080 confirmed measles cases across the country as of Thursday.
The cases have far surpassed 2025's total number of cases, which was 2,289. Last year had seen the most cases in three decades.
Most states and Washington, D.C., have reported cases of the contagious disease.
This week, Pennsylvania surpassed 1,000 total cases this year after reporting on Wednesday 145 new cases.
According to Pennsylvania's Health Department, there have been five measles-associated deaths in the state this year. The state considers a death to be associated with measles when a person dies within 30 days of experiencing symptoms with clinical evidence of an infection and a positive lab test, and when the death isn't due to unrelated causes like a car accident.
In neighboring New York, Gov. Kathy Hochul declared an emergency Monday over the increasing number of measles cases in the region. Hochul issued an executive order allowing more healthcare professionals to administer measles vaccines and letting nurses order testing, according to the governor's office.
According to the CDC, 95% of patients nationwide this year were unvaccinated against the disease or their vaccination status was not known. About 2% of patients had received one dose of the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine, and another 2% had received two doses.
Measles symptoms typically appear between one and two weeks after people come in contact with the disease, according to the CDC. The initial symptoms include high fever, cough, runny nose, and red, watery eyes.
Two to three days later, tiny white spots may appear inside the mouth, according to the CDC. A rash then breaks out within three to five days after the initial symptoms.

articles.content_orig:
Saturday night's massive SEC clash between the No. 2 Georgia Bulldogs and No. 6 Alabama Crimson Tide at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, may avoid the wrath of Hurricane Isaias.
According to The Weather Channel , Saturday's forecast for Tuscaloosa looks surprisingly tame at and around the time the game is scheduled to be played at 7:30 p.m. ET.
Although heavy rain and possible "tropical storm conditions" are expected throughout the morning, the chance of rain drops to 24 percent at around 10 a.m. and stays there until around 9 p.m. when it increases to a 36 percent chance of light rain.
Winds fewer than 10 mph are expected throughout the game as well, so that shouldn't be much of a factor either.
To this point, all signs suggest the game will be played as scheduled with no announced plans to change the time or location.
On Wednesday, Alabama Athletics released a statement on X, noting that the school was monitoring the weather and still planned to hold the game as scheduled:
As of Friday, The Weather Channel reported that Hurricane Isaias was a Category 3 hurricane located 240 miles south of Pensacola, Florida.
The expectation is that Hurricane Isaias will make landfall late Friday night from "Alabama to the western Florida Panhandle."
Hurricane Isaias is expected to "move farther inland and weaken" by Saturday, and radar appears to show it moving to the northern part of Alabama, just clear of Tuscaloosa.
Given the enormity of Saturday's game, the forecast comes as a major relief, as it doesn't appear rain and wind will have a significant impact.
Georgia and Alabama are tied atop the SEC right now with matching 3-0 conference records and 5-0 overall records, meaning the winner will have a huge advantage over the loser in terms of positioning for a potential SEC Championship Game berth.

articles.title_orig: Prize-winning image which sparked backlash was AI-generated, Nikon rules
articles.title_zh: Prize-winning image which sparked backlash was AI-generated, Nikon rules
articles.content_orig:
The winner of a prestigious scientific photography competition has been disqualified following concerns raised by other scientists that it was fake.
Nikon said the use of generative AI in the composition of the video broke the rules of its Small World In Motion contest, which accepts photos and video taken using powerful microscopes.
The firm said the video "did not comply with the competition rules regarding generative AI", but added it was not a judgement of the entrant's professional reputation or scientific contributions.
It said it would now look at the rules and procedures of the annual contest, which has been running for 15 years and is specifically for microscopic images.
Nikon said it came to the decision "after thoroughly re-evaluating the video and supporting materials and consulting with members of our judging panel".
The winning entry came from Dr Ning Xu, from Tsinghua University in China, who submitted a short video showing tiny, hair-like structures called cilia moving in the airway of a child with the respiratory condition PCD.
The BBC has approached him for comment.
A number of scientists, including former competition judges, complained to Nikon on its LinkedIn page that the video did not appear to be real.
Xu had acknowledged using AI, but said he believed he had acted within the rules, and had cooperated with Nikon's investigation.
University of Leicester scientist Dr Robert Hirst, who was among the first experts to voice concerns, said he was "not surprised" and he "knew immediately that the video was fabricated".
"I have been diagnosing PCD for 20 years by examining their cilia waveform, length, cell size and shape," he said.
Hirst, who is lead scientist for the NHS centre for PCD diagnosis at the university, said the cells and cilia "look nothing like those from PCD patients".
"This controversy has impacted a lot of patients, scientists, doctors and PCD support networks around the world," he said.

articles.title_orig: Longtime California wheat geneticist receives World Agriculture Prize
articles.title_zh: Longtime California wheat geneticist receives World Agriculture Prize
articles.content_orig:
Published 8:30 am Friday, October 9, 2026
Longtime University of California wheat geneticist Jorge Dubcovsky has been named the 2026 World Agriculture Prize Laureate.
Dubcovsky received the award in the category for countries that have a developed economy from the Global Confederation of Higher Education Associations for the Agricultural and Life Sciences (GCHERA).
“It is a nice recognition by peers of the value of our work,” Dubcovsky told Capital Press.
He most enjoys planning new experiments, discovering new things, and “interacting with curious and intelligent young people every day!”
“Dubcovsky is internationally recognized as one of the world’s most influential wheat geneticists,” GCHERA said in a press release. “For more than three decades, Dubcovsky has led innovative research that has significantly advanced scientific understanding of wheat biology and accelerated the application of genomic technologies in crop improvement.”
Dubcovsky’s work has been instrumental in identifying and characterizing key genes controlling yield, disease resistance, flowering time, nutrient use efficiency and adaptation to diverse growing environments, the organization stated.
“These discoveries have been widely adopted by breeding programs and have contributed to the development of improved wheat varieties cultivated on millions of hectares worldwide,” the GCHERA press release states.
Dubcovsky reported that UC Davis’ small grains breeding program is “doing very well.”
“New, young and energetic professor” Xiaofei Zhang is taking over Dubcovsky’s previous breeding program responsibilities; “we are collaborating closely and effectively.”
The program is developing dual-purpose wheat varieties for forage and good breadmaking quality, as requested by California wheat farmers.
“This will give growers more flexibility on where to sell their harvest,” Dubcovsky said.
Zhang has a new USDA grant to investigate new dwarfing genes developed in Dubcovsky’s lab to improve wheat yield “beyond the gains of the first green revolution.”
Former PhD. and postdoctoral student Josh Hegarty leads daily breeding operations and making “good inroads” with triticale varieties, Dubcovsky said. The university’s triticale varieties Bopak and Atrea are being used “extensively,” and Hegarty is releasing three new varieties. In the pipeline are awn-less varieties and varieties with improved breadmaking quality.
The industry’s biggest needs, according to Dubcovsky:
1. Dual-purpose varieties intended for grain production and livestock forage.
2. “We need to keep our varieties resistant to emerging pathogens and keep an eye on a new race of stripe rust that defeated one of the two major resistance genes Yr5 and Yr15 we have currently deployed.”
4. “Without forgetting quality,” Dubcovsky said. “We need them all for successful varieties.”
Dubcovsky thanked farmers for their support for the last 28 years.
“Grower’s funds are essential to keep the breeding program running, since that part is not paid by UC Davis or USDA,” he said. “This is a perfect collaboration: Growers provide support to develop their varieties; UC Davis provides knowledge, breeders and facilities; USDA provides funds for research and innovation. If each of us keep doing his part, we have a bright future.”
Dubcovsky will be formally honored during the 2026 World Agriculture Prize Award Ceremony Oct. 28 at Nanjing Agricultural University in China.
